sections.bodyEn: From the great heaven she set her mind on the great below. From the great heaven the goddess set her mind on the great below; Inana set her mind on the great below. My mistress abandoned heaven, abandoned earth, and descended to the netherworld. She abandoned the office of en and of lagar. She abandoned the E-ana in Unug, and her temples in Bad-tibira, Zabalam, Adab, Nibru and Kiš, and the E-ulmaš in Agade — seven temples in seven cities — and went down to the netherworld.
sections.bodyZh: 从伟大的天上，她把心思转向了伟大的地下。女神从伟大的天上，把心思转向了伟大的地下。伊南娜从伟大的天上，把心思转向了伟大的地下。我的女主人舍弃了天空，舍弃了大地，走向冥界。她舍弃了“恩”的祭司之职，舍弃了“拉加尔”的祭司之职，走向冥界。她舍弃了乌鲁克的伊安那神庙，舍弃了巴德提比拉的神庙、扎巴拉姆的吉古那神庙、阿达布的神庙、尼普尔的神庙、基什的神庙，还有阿卡德的伊乌尔马什神庙——一共七座城市的七座神庙，独自走向冥界。
sections.headingEn: From the great above to the great below

sections.bodyEn: Inana gathered the seven divine powers and held them in her hand. She put the šugura, the turban of the open country, on her head, a wig on her brow, small lapis lazuli beads around her neck and twin egg-shaped beads on her breast. She wrapped her body in the pala dress, the garment of ladyship, painted her eyes with the ointment called 'Let a man come, let him come', bound on the pectoral called 'Come, man, come', slipped a gold ring on her hand and held the lapis lazuli measuring rod and line.
sections.bodyZh: 伊南娜取下七种神力，把它们收集在手中，放在手边。她头上戴着平原上的“舒古拉”王冠，额前垂着假发，脖子上挂着小粒的青金石项链，胸前佩着一对蛋形的珠子，身上裹着象征女主人身份的“帕拉”长袍，眼睛涂上一种叫作“让男人来吧，让他来吧”的眼影，胸前系着一块叫作“男人啊，来吧”的胸饰，手上戴着金指环，手里拿着青金石的量杆和测绳。就这样，她穿戴整齐，向冥界走去。

sections.bodyEn: As Inana went, she told her minister Ninšubur: my faithful minister, I am going down to the netherworld. When I have arrived there, make a lament for me in the ruins, beat the drum for me in the assembly, go round the houses of the gods; lacerate your eyes, mouth and thighs, dress in a single garment like a pauper. Then go alone to Enlil in the E-kur at Nibru and weep: Father Enlil, don't let your daughter be put to death in the netherworld. If Enlil does not help, go to Nanna in Urim; if Nanna does not help, go to Enki in Eridug. Father Enki, who knows the plant of life and the water of life, will surely not let me die.
sections.bodyZh: 伊南娜一边走，一边对她的大臣宁舒布尔说：我忠实的大臣，说话可靠的使者，我现在要下到冥界去。我到了冥界以后，你要在废墟中为我敲起鼓，在议会的厅堂里为我哭泣，在众神的家中为我奔走哀告；你要抓伤你的眼睛、你的嘴、你的大腿，像穷人一样只穿一件衣服。然后你独自一人，先到尼普尔的埃库尔神庙去，在恩利尔面前哭诉：父亲恩利尔，不要让你的女儿死在冥界！如果恩利尔不帮你，你就去乌尔，到南纳那里去哭诉；如果南纳也不帮你，你就去埃利都，到恩基那里去哭诉。父亲恩基，那位深知一切的神，知道生命之草、生命之水，他一定不会让我死去。

sections.bodyEn: At the palace Ganzer Inana pushed aggressively on the door and shouted: open up, doorman! Neti, open up, I shall enter alone! Neti, chief doorman of the netherworld, asked who she was. She was Inana going to the east, she said. Why then, asked Neti, had she come to the land of no return? Because, she said, Gud-gal-ana, the husband of her elder sister Ereškigala, had died, and she had come to his funeral rites. Neti went to report. Ereškigala slapped her thigh, bit her lip and took the matter to heart; she ordered the seven gates bolted and each door of the palace opened only a crack, so that Inana would enter crouching and be stripped as she came.
sections.bodyZh: 伊南娜来到冥界的宫殿“甘泽尔”前，用力推门，在门口大声喊道：守门人，开门！守门人，开门！内提，开门，我独自一人要进去！冥界的首席守门人内提问她：你是谁？伊南娜说：我是天上的伊南娜，要到太阳升起的地方去。内提说：你若是天上的伊南娜，要到太阳升起的地方去，为什么到这条有去无回的路上来？伊南娜说：因为我的姐姐埃列什基伽勒的丈夫、天牛古伽拉纳死了，我来参加他的葬礼宴会。内提让她等着，去向冥后埃列什基伽勒报告。埃列什基伽勒听了，拍着大腿，咬着嘴唇，把这件事放在心上，然后吩咐内提：把冥界的七道门都闩上，把冥界宫殿的门一扇一扇地打开一条缝；让她弯下腰进来，进门时脱去她的王者服饰。
sections.headingEn: At the gate of the netherworld

sections.bodyEn: Neti bolted the seven gates and opened the palace door a crack: come, Inana, enter. At the first gate the turban was removed from her head. 'What is this?' 'Be satisfied, Inana, a divine power of the netherworld has been fulfilled. Inana, you must not open your mouth against the rites of the netherworld.' At the second gate the lapis beads were removed from her neck; at the third the egg-shaped beads; at the fourth the pectoral; at the fifth the gold ring; at the sixth the measuring rod and line; and at the seventh the pala dress, the garment of ladyship. Each time she asked, and each time the same answer came.
sections.bodyZh: 内提照吩咐闩上了七道门，又把宫殿的门打开一条缝，对伊南娜说：来吧，伊南娜，进来吧。她走进第一道门时，头上的王冠被取走了。她问：这是怎么回事？内提回答：满足吧，伊南娜，冥界的神力已经实现了。伊南娜，在冥界的仪式中你不能开口。走进第二道门时，脖子上的青金石项链被取走了；第三道门，胸前的蛋形珠子被取走了；第四道门，胸饰被取走了；第五道门，手上的金指环被取走了；第六道门，青金石的量杆和测绳被取走了；第七道门，她身上那件象征女主人身份的帕拉长袍也被取走了。每一次她发问，得到的都是同样的回答：满足吧，伊南娜，冥界的神力已经实现了。

sections.bodyEn: After she had crouched down and her clothes had been removed, they were carried away. Then her sister Ereškigala rose from her throne, and Inana sat on the throne instead. The Anuna, the seven judges, rendered their decision against her. Ereškigala looked at her with the look of death, spoke to her with the speech of anger, shouted at her with the shout of heavy guilt. The afflicted woman was turned into a corpse, and the corpse was hung on a hook.
sections.bodyZh: 伊南娜弯着腰、赤身裸体地走了进去。她的姐姐埃列什基伽勒从王座上站了起来，伊南娜就在王座上坐下了。冥界的七位审判官——阿努纳众神，对她作出了判决。埃列什基伽勒用死亡的目光盯着她，对她说出愤怒的话语，对她喊出罪恶的叫声。伊南娜被打倒了，变成了一具尸体，那具尸体被挂在了钩子上。这是整首诗中最冷酷的一刻：天上的女王、带着七件神力走下冥界的伊南娜，转眼之间就成了钩子上的一具尸体。冥界的门已经关上，在那里没有人能替她求情。可是她临行前早有安排——在地上，还有一个人在等着她。

sections.bodyEn: After three days and three nights had passed, Ninšubur did as her mistress had ordered: she lamented in the ruins, beat the drum in the assembly, went round the gods' houses, lacerated her eyes, mouth and thighs and dressed like a pauper. Alone she went to the E-kur and wept before Enlil: don't let your precious metal be alloyed with the dust of the netherworld, don't let your lapis be split by the stone-cutter, don't let young lady Inana be put to death. Father Enlil angrily replied that his daughter craved the great heaven and the great below; whoever obtains the divine powers of the netherworld remains there. Enlil would not help, and Nanna in Urim likewise refused.
sections.bodyZh: 三天三夜过去了，伊南娜没有回来，她的大臣宁舒布尔照女主人的吩咐，在废墟中为她哀哭，在议会厅里为她敲鼓，在众神的家中奔走，抓伤自己的眼睛、嘴和大腿，像穷人一样只穿一件衣服。她独自来到尼普尔的埃库尔神庙，在恩利尔面前哭诉：父亲恩利尔，不要让你的女儿死在冥界！不要让你宝贵的金属在冥界的尘土里被弄脏，不要让你宝贵的青金石被石匠的石头劈碎，不要让少女伊南娜死在冥界！可是恩利尔大怒说：我的女儿渴望伟大的天上，又渴望伟大的地下。冥界的神力是不能贪求的，谁去了那里，谁就得留在那里！恩利尔不肯帮忙。宁舒布尔又去了乌尔的南纳那里，南纳也同样拒绝了她。

sections.bodyEn: Ninšubur went to Eridug and wept before Enki. Father Enki answered: what has my daughter done? She has me worried! What has Inana done? She has me worried! He removed some dirt from the tip of one fingernail and created the kur-ĝara; from the other he created the gala-tura. To one he gave the life-giving plant, to the other the life-giving water. Flit past the door like flies, he told them; slip through the door pivots like phantoms. The mother who gave birth, Ereškigala, lies there in pain because of her children, her shoulders and breast uncovered. When she cries 'Oh my heart!', say 'You are troubled, our mistress, oh your heart!' She will offer you the river and the fields; refuse them, and ask for the corpse hanging on the hook.
sections.bodyZh: 宁舒布尔来到埃利都，在恩基面前哭诉。父亲恩基回答说：我的女儿做了什么？她让我心焦！伊南娜做了什么？她让我心焦！所有土地的女主人做了什么？天上的圣女做了什么？她让我心焦！恩基从一只手指甲的尖上取下一点泥垢，造出了“库尔加拉”；又从另一只手指甲的尖上取下一点泥垢，造出了“加拉图拉”。他把生命之草交给库尔加拉，把生命之水交给加拉图拉，嘱咐它们：像苍蝇一样绕着门飞，像蛇一样从门轴下溜进去。那位生育者的母亲埃列什基伽勒正因为孩子的缘故躺在那里，没有衣服遮盖她圣洁的肩膀，没有亚麻布遮盖她的胸膛，她会喊“哎呀，我的里面！”，你们就跟着说“哎呀，你的里面！”；她喊“哎呀，我的外面！”，你们就说“哎呀，你的外面！”她会因此高兴，送给你们河水和田里的谷物，你们都不要接受，只要求她把挂在钩子上的那具尸体交给你们。

sections.bodyEn: They did as Enki said, slipping in like flies and phantoms. When the queen cried 'Oh my heart!', they answered 'You are troubled, our mistress, oh your heart!', and so with 'oh my liver'. Who are you? she asked; if gods, I will speak with you, if mortals, I will decree a destiny for you. She made them swear and offered the river with its water and the field with its grain, and they refused. Give us the corpse hanging on the hook, they said. That is the corpse of your queen. Whether it is our king's or our queen's, give it to us. The corpse was handed over; one sprinkled the life-giving plant on it, the other the life-giving water, and so Inana arose.
sections.bodyZh: 两个小人照恩基的吩咐，像苍蝇一样绕着门飞，像幽灵一样从门轴下溜了进去。冥后正痛苦地躺着，她喊“哎呀，我的里面”，它们就说“你很痛苦，我们的女主人，哎呀，你的里面”；她喊“哎呀，我的外面”，它们就说“哎呀，你的外面”。埃列什基伽勒问：你们是谁？我要祝福你们，你们是神，我要和你们说话；你们是人，我要给你们定下命运。她让它们以天地的名义发誓，送给它们满河的水，它们不要；送给它们满田的谷物，它们也不要。它们说：请把挂在钩子上的那具尸体给我们吧。冥后说：那是你们女主人的尸体。它们说：不论是我们国王的还是我们女主人的，都请给我们吧。尸体被交给了它们。一个把生命之草撒在尸体上，另一个把生命之水洒在尸体上。于是，伊南娜站了起来。

sections.bodyEn: As Inana was about to ascend, the Anuna seized her: who has ever ascended from the netherworld unscathed? If Inana is to ascend, let her provide a substitute. So the galla demons went up with her — the one in front holding a sceptre though not a minister, the one beside her bearing a weapon though not a warrior. These are demons who know no food, know no drink, eat no flour offering and drink no libation, accept no gifts, enjoy no lovemaking and kiss no children; they tear the wife from a man's embrace and the child from its mother's breast.
sections.bodyZh: 伊南娜正要从冥界上去，阿努纳众神抓住了她，说：有谁从冥界上去，能够安然无恙？如果伊南娜要从冥界上去，就让她提供一个替身来代替她！于是一群“加拉”恶魔跟着她一起上去。走在她前面的那个，手里拿着权杖，却不是大臣；走在她身边的那个，腰间佩着武器，却不是战士。这些恶魔不知道食物，不知道饮水，不吃撒下的面粉，不喝倒出的清水，不收礼物；它们从不享受夫妻的欢乐，不亲吻可爱的孩子；它们从男人膝上夺走妻子，从母亲胸前夺走孩子。

sections.bodyEn: As Inana came out, Ninšubur threw herself at her feet, covered in dust and dressed in a filthy garment. The demons said: we will take her. Inana refused: she is my minister of fair words, who did not forget my instructions, who lamented in the ruins, beat the drum and went round the gods' houses — she brought me back to life; how could I give her to you? At Umma, Šara threw himself at her feet in a filthy garment; at Bad-tibira, Lulal did the same. Each time the demons asked to take them, and each time Inana refused, because they had mourned for her.
sections.bodyZh: 伊南娜走出冥界，宁舒布尔扑倒在她脚下，身上满是灰尘，穿着肮脏的衣服。恶魔们说：走吧，伊南娜，我们要把她带走。伊南娜说：她是我说话可靠的大臣，是忠实的使者，她没有忘记我的吩咐，在废墟中为我哀哭，在议会厅里为我敲鼓，在众神的家中为我奔走。是她让我活了过来，我怎么能把她交给你们？她们来到乌玛，沙拉神穿着肮脏的衣服，在自己的神庙里扑倒在伊南娜脚下；来到巴德提比拉，卢拉尔神也穿着肮脏的衣服扑倒在她脚下。恶魔们每次都说要把他们带走，伊南娜都说：他是我的歌者、我的侍从，他为我哀悼，不能给你们。于是这几位都得到了赦免。

sections.bodyEn: Beneath the great apple tree of Kul-aba they found Dumuzid, Inana's husband, clothed in a magnificent garment and seated on a magnificent throne, not mourning. The demons seized him by the thighs, spilled his seven churns and silenced the shepherd's pipe. Inana looked at him with the look of death, spoke the speech of anger: take him away! Dumuzid turned pale and wept, raised his hands to Utu: you are my brother-in-law and I your sister's husband; I carried cream to your mother's house. Change my hands into snake's hands and my feet into snake's feet, so I may escape my demons. Utu accepted his tears and changed his hands and feet, and Dumuzid escaped. The broken ending says Dumuzid will spend half the year below and his sister Geštin-ana the other half.
sections.bodyZh: 她们来到库拉巴的大苹果树下，看见伊南娜的丈夫杜木兹穿着华丽的衣服，坐在高高的王座上，没有为她哀悼。恶魔们扑上去，抓住他的大腿，打翻他的七只奶桶，不让牧人再吹奏他的芦笛。伊南娜用死亡的目光盯着他，对他说出愤怒的话语，喊出罪恶的叫声：就是他，把他带走！杜木兹吓得脸色苍白，痛哭起来，他向天上举起双手，向太阳神乌图祈祷：乌图啊，你是我的朋友，我是你的妹夫；我把奶油带到你母亲的家，把牛奶带到宁加尔的家。请把我的手变成蛇的手，把我的脚变成蛇的脚，让我从恶魔手里逃走，不让它们抓住我。乌图接受了他的眼泪，把他的手变成蛇的手，把他的脚变成蛇的脚，杜木兹便从恶魔手中逃脱了。故事的结尾残缺不全，可以读出的部分说：杜木兹在冥界待半年，他的姐姐盖什提南娜待另外半年。
sections.uncertaintyNote: 结尾诗行残缺；杜木兹与盖什提南娜各在冥界半年的安排依据可读出的部分，其他苏美尔作品另有不同讲法。

stories.canonicalTitle: Marduk and Tiamat
stories.editorialNote: 待电子巴比伦图书馆各泥板逐行拆分后扩充。
stories.summaryEn: The registered layer of Enuma elish confirms Marduk and Tiamat in the creation combat; this version is an evidence guide and does not promote unmodeled details to structured fact.
stories.summaryZh: 《埃努玛·埃利什》的登记层确认马尔杜克与提亚马特参与创世战斗；本版先提供证据导读，不把未逐条录入的战斗细节写成结构化事实。
stories.titleZh: 马尔杜克与提亚马特

claims.statement: Before heaven and earth were named, Apsû and Tiamat mingle their waters, and from them are born Lahmu and Lahamu, Anshar and Kishar, Anu and Ea.
Disturbed by the young gods' noise, Apsû plots with his vizier Mummu to destroy them, though Tiamat objects to destroying their own offspring.
Ea puts Apsû to sleep with a pure incantation, takes his crown and aura, kills him and builds his own dwelling upon him.
Marduk is born to Ea and Damkina with four eyes and four ears and fiery lips; Anu gives him the four winds, with which he troubles Tiamat.
Urged to avenge Apsû, Tiamat brings forth eleven monsters, makes Qingu commander of her host and fastens the Tablet of Destinies on his breast.
After Ea and Anu both turn back from Tiamat, Marduk offers to fight her on condition that the gods make his word decree destinies.
At a banquet summoned by Anshar, the great gods eat, drink and then assemble to decree Marduk's destiny as their avenger.
The gods test Marduk's word by having him make a garment vanish and reappear, then proclaim him king and give him sceptre, throne and weapon.
Marduk arms himself with bow, mace, lightning, a net held by the four winds, seven destructive winds, the Flood-weapon and a storm chariot drawn by four poisonous steeds.
In single combat Marduk nets Tiamat, drives the evil wind into her open mouth and shoots an arrow through her belly and heart.
Captured by Marduk after Tiamat's fall, Qingu is stripped of the Tablet of Destinies, which Marduk seals and fastens on his own breast.
Marduk splits Tiamat's body like a dried fish, making the sky from one half and the earth from the other, opening the Tigris and Euphrates from her eyes and ordering stars, months and the moon.
On Marduk's plan Ea creates humankind from the blood of the condemned Qingu, so that humans bear the gods' toil.
The Anunnaki build Babylon and the temple Esagila for Marduk, and the gods proclaim his fifty names.

entities.nameZh: 马尔杜克与提亚马特之战

events.summaryEn: When on high the heaven had not been named and below the earth had not been called by name, there was only Apsû, the begetter, and Tiamat, who bore them all, mingling their waters.
events.summaryZh: 当上面的天空还没有名字，下面的大地还没有被叫出名字的时候，只有生育众神的阿普苏——甜水，和生下一切的提亚马特——咸水，把他们的水混合在一起。
events.titleEn: When on high the heaven had not been named
events.titleZh: 天地还没有名字的时候

events.summaryEn: The young gods banded together and churned back and forth, disturbing Tiamat's belly with their din.
events.summaryZh: 年轻的神们聚在一起，来回嬉闹，搅动了提亚马特的腹部，他们的喧哗让她不得安宁。

events.summaryEn: When the gods heard the plan they ran about in panic and then fell silent.
events.summaryZh: 众神听说了这个计划，惊慌失措，四处乱跑，然后陷入沉默。

events.summaryEn: In the chamber of destinies, the shrine of designs, Marduk was born, most able and wisest of gods.
events.summaryZh: 就在那座命运之屋、众神之殿里，最能干、最睿智的神诞生了——他就是马尔杜克。

events.summaryEn: The gods troubled by the winds reproached Tiamat: when Apsû was slain she did nothing, and now Anu's winds churn her belly and they cannot sleep.
events.summaryZh: 被风搅得不得安宁的众神来到提亚马特面前，责怪她说：当他们杀死你的丈夫阿普苏时，你袖手旁观；现在安努又造出四方的风，搅乱你的腹部，让我们也睡不着觉。

events.summaryEn: Ea, hearing Tiamat's plans, was struck dumb, then went to his grandfather Anshar, who beat his thigh and bit his lip in anxiety.
events.summaryZh: 埃阿听说提亚马特的部署，惊得说不出话来，过了很久才平静下来，去向祖父安沙尔报告。
events.titleEn: No god dares to face her

events.summaryEn: Anshar sent his messenger Kakka to Lahmu and Lahamu to repeat all Tiamat's preparations, the gods' fear and Marduk's condition, and to summon the gods to decree Marduk's destiny.
events.summaryZh: 安沙尔把他的使者卡卡叫来，派他去找拉赫穆和拉哈穆，把提亚马特的种种部署、众神的恐惧和马尔杜克的条件原原本本地重复一遍，请众神都来集会，为马尔杜克决定命运。

events.summaryEn: The gods set up a princely dais for Marduk, and he sat before his fathers to receive kingship.
events.summaryZh: 众神为马尔杜克设立了一座王者的宝座，他坐在父辈们面前，接受统治的权力。

events.summaryEn: Marduk made a bow and appointed it his weapon, set the arrow and fitted the string; he took the mace in his right hand and hung bow and quiver at his side.
events.summaryZh: 马尔杜克做好了出征的准备：他造了一张弓，把它作为自己的武器，搭上箭，系紧弓弦；他右手拿起权杖，把弓和箭袋挂在身侧。

events.summaryEn: Marduk went straight towards Tiamat and watched for Qingu's scheme.
events.summaryZh: 马尔杜克径直走向提亚马特，注视着金古的计谋。

events.summaryEn: When Tiamat was slain, the gods who marched with her broke ranks and fled to save their lives, but they were surrounded with no escape.
events.summaryZh: 提亚马特一死，跟随她的众神四散奔逃，想要保住性命，可是他们被团团围住，无处可逃。
events.titleEn: The captives and the Tablet of Destinies

events.summaryEn: Marduk returned to Tiamat, crushed her skull with his mace, cut her arteries and let the north wind carry her blood away.
events.summaryZh: 马尔杜克回到提亚马特的身边，用无情的权杖砸碎了她的头骨，割断她的血管，让北风把她的血吹到隐秘的地方。
events.titleEn: Heaven and earth from her body
events.uncertaintyNote: 第五块泥板长期残缺，后来出土的抄本补足了部分诗行；本站按 eBL 综合文本概述。

events.summaryEn: The gods asked Marduk to decide their toil.
events.summaryZh: 众神请马尔杜克决定他们的劳役。

events.summaryEn: The freed Anunnaki offered to build Marduk a shrine where they too might rest.
events.summaryZh: 被解放的阿努纳众神对马尔杜克说：我们要为你建一座圣所，作为你的居所，让我们在其中安歇。

sections.bodyEn: When on high the heaven had not been named and below the earth had not been called by name, there was only Apsû, the begetter, and Tiamat, who bore them all, mingling their waters. No reed hut had been matted, no marsh had appeared, no god had been brought into being, named or given a destiny. Then gods were born within them: Lahmu and Lahamu; then Anshar and Kishar, greater than they; then Anu, equal to his fathers, and Anu begot Nudimmud, that is Ea, wiser and stronger than all his ancestors.
sections.bodyZh: 当上面的天空还没有名字，下面的大地还没有被叫出名字的时候，只有生育众神的阿普苏——甜水，和生下一切的提亚马特——咸水，把他们的水混合在一起。那时还没有芦苇搭的小屋，还没有沼泽地，还没有任何一位神出现，没有名字，也没有命运。就在这混合的水中，众神诞生了：最先是拉赫穆和拉哈穆，他们长大以后，又生出安沙尔和基沙尔，安沙尔和基沙尔又生下了天神安努。安努与他的父辈一样强大，他又生出了与自己相像的努迪穆德——也就是埃阿。埃阿比他的父辈都更聪明、更有智慧、更有力量。
sections.headingEn: When on high the heaven had not been named
sections.headingZh: 天地还没有名字的时候

sections.bodyEn: The young gods banded together and churned back and forth, disturbing Tiamat's belly with their din. Apsû could not quiet them, and Tiamat kept silent. Apsû summoned his vizier Mummu and went to Tiamat: their ways are loathsome to me, he said; by day I cannot rest, by night I cannot sleep; I will destroy them so that silence returns and we may sleep. Tiamat cried out in anger: why should we destroy what we ourselves made? Their ways are troublesome, but let us bear it kindly. Yet Mummu urged Apsû on, and his face grew bright at the evil he planned against his children.
sections.bodyZh: 年轻的神们聚在一起，来回嬉闹，搅动了提亚马特的腹部，他们的喧哗让她不得安宁。阿普苏无法让他们安静下来，提亚马特也默不作声。于是阿普苏召来他的大臣穆姆，两人一起去找提亚马特商量。阿普苏说：他们的所作所为让我讨厌，白天不能休息，夜里不能睡觉。我要毁掉他们，结束他们的行为，让一切重归寂静，我们好安睡。提亚马特听了大怒，大声喊道：我们为什么要毁掉自己生下的孩子？他们的行为虽然让人烦恼，我们还是要宽厚地忍耐。可是穆姆劝阿普苏坚持他的计划，阿普苏听了喜形于色，因为他想着要对自己的子孙下手。

sections.bodyEn: When the gods heard the plan they ran about in panic and then fell silent. Only Ea, who knows everything, saw through it. He made a pure incantation, recited it and poured sleep over Apsû, and made Mummu drowsy. He loosed Apsû's band, took off his crown and his radiant aura and put them on himself; he bound Apsû and killed him, and tied Mummu by a nose-rope. Then he founded his dwelling upon Apsû, named it Apsû, and lived there in peace with his wife Damkina.
sections.bodyZh: 众神听说了这个计划，惊慌失措，四处乱跑，然后陷入沉默。只有无所不知、智慧超群的埃阿看透了一切。他想出了一个大计：他编了一道纯净的咒语，念给阿普苏听，让他沉沉睡去，又让大臣穆姆也昏昏欲睡。埃阿解下阿普苏的腰带，摘下他的王冠，取走他光芒四射的神光，自己戴上；他捆住阿普苏，把他杀死；又把穆姆用绳子拴住，牵着他的鼻绳。然后，埃阿在阿普苏的身体上建起了自己的住所，把它叫作“阿普苏”，并在那里设立了圣殿，与他的妻子达姆金娜一起住在其中，享受安宁。

sections.bodyEn: In the chamber of destinies, the shrine of designs, Marduk was born, most able and wisest of gods. Ea his father begot him, Damkina his mother bore him; he sucked the breasts of goddesses and was filled with awesome radiance. His stature was lofty, his eyes flashed, he was mature from birth. Anu, seeing him, rejoiced and gave him double godhead: four eyes and four ears, and when his lips moved fire blazed forth. Anu made the four winds and gave them to him to play with; he raised dust and stirred up floods, troubling Tiamat day and night.
sections.bodyZh: 就在那座命运之屋、众神之殿里，最能干、最睿智的神诞生了——他就是马尔杜克。他的父亲埃阿生下他，母亲达姆金娜怀着他。他吮吸女神的乳汁长大，周身充满了令人敬畏的光辉。他的身材高挑，眼睛闪闪发光，一出生就像成年人一样威武。他的祖父安努看见他，满心欢喜，赐给他双倍的神性：他有四只眼睛、四只耳朵，嘴唇一动就喷出火焰，什么都看得见，什么都听得见。他比众神都高大，四肢比例完美，令人无法理解。安努还造出四方的风交给他玩耍；马尔杜克用这些风掀起尘土、卷起洪水，搅得提亚马特日夜不安。

sections.bodyEn: The gods troubled by the winds reproached Tiamat: when Apsû was slain she did nothing, and now Anu's winds churn her belly and they cannot sleep. Will she not avenge Apsû? Tiamat was persuaded and prepared for war. Mother Hubur, who forms all things, bore eleven monsters: giant serpents with poison for blood, fierce dragons cloaked in terror, the viper, the dragon, the hairy hero, the great lion, the mad dog, the scorpion-man, fierce demons, the fish-man and the bull-man. She exalted Qingu among the gods, made him commander, fastened the Tablet of Destinies on his breast and said: your command shall not be changed.
sections.bodyZh: 被风搅得不得安宁的众神来到提亚马特面前，责怪她说：当他们杀死你的丈夫阿普苏时，你袖手旁观；现在安努又造出四方的风，搅乱你的腹部，让我们也睡不着觉。你难道不为阿普苏报仇吗？提亚马特被说动了，她决心开战。万物之母提亚马特生出了十一种可怕的怪物：毒牙锋利的巨蛇，身上流着毒液而不是血；凶猛的龙，周身披着恐怖的光辉，让看见的人立刻倒下；还有毒蛇、龙、长毛的怪物、巨大的狮子、狂怒的狗、蝎人、狂暴的风魔、鱼人和牛人。她在众神中抬举了金古，让他做军队的统帅，把命运泥板交给他，挂在他的胸前，对他说：你的命令永不改变，你的话就是法律。
sections.evidenceNote: 《埃努玛·埃利什》第一至二块泥板。

sections.bodyEn: Ea, hearing Tiamat's plans, was struck dumb, then went to his grandfather Anshar, who beat his thigh and bit his lip in anxiety. Anshar sent Ea, who turned back at the sight of her; then Anu, who saw her array halfway and returned saying his strength could not overcome her. The gods sat in silence, thinking no god could face Tiamat. Then Ea called his son Marduk and sent him before Anshar. Marduk said: I will go and fulfil your desire. But if I defeat Tiamat and save your lives, convene the assembly and proclaim my destiny supreme: let my word, like yours, decree fates; let what I create never be altered and what I command never be revoked.
sections.bodyZh: 埃阿听说提亚马特的部署，惊得说不出话来，过了很久才平静下来，去向祖父安沙尔报告。安沙尔捶着大腿，咬着嘴唇，心中不安。他先派埃阿去平息提亚马特，埃阿看见她的军威，心生畏惧，退了回来；他又派安努去，安努走到半路，望见提亚马特的布置，也不敢上前，转身回来说：我的力量不足以制服她。众神坐在那里，默不作声，人人都觉得没有一位神能与提亚马特对抗。这时埃阿把儿子马尔杜克叫到身边，对他说：去吧，到安沙尔面前去，站在那里，看着他，他会安心的。马尔杜克来到安沙尔面前说：我愿意出战，替你们报仇。可是如果我战胜提亚马特、救了你们的性命，你们必须召开大会，宣布我的命运至高无上：让我开口就能像你们一样决定命运，我所创造的永不改变，我说出的话永不收回。
sections.headingEn: No god dares to face her

sections.bodyEn: Anshar sent his messenger Kakka to Lahmu and Lahamu to repeat all Tiamat's preparations, the gods' fear and Marduk's condition, and to summon the gods to decree Marduk's destiny. Lahmu and Lahamu cried out that they could not understand Tiamat's deeds. All the great gods came before Anshar; they kissed one another in the assembly, ate bread and drank sweet wine and beer until their bodies relaxed and their hearts were merry, and then decreed the destiny of Marduk, their avenger.
sections.bodyZh: 安沙尔把他的使者卡卡叫来，派他去找拉赫穆和拉哈穆，把提亚马特的种种部署、众神的恐惧和马尔杜克的条件原原本本地重复一遍，请众神都来集会，为马尔杜克决定命运。拉赫穆和拉哈穆听了，大声惊叫：提亚马特为什么变成这样，我们实在不明白！所有的大神都来到安沙尔面前，他们彼此亲吻，在集会中坐下，吃着面包，喝着甜酒，啤酒让他们的身体放松，他们无忧无虑，心情愉快，于是为他们的复仇者马尔杜克决定命运。

sections.bodyEn: The gods set up a princely dais for Marduk, and he sat before his fathers to receive kingship. You are the most honoured of the great gods, they said; your command is Anu's; from this day your word shall not be changed, to raise and to lower is in your hand. To prove his word decreed fate, they set a garment in their midst: at his word let it be destroyed, at his word let it be whole again. He spoke and it vanished; he spoke again and it reappeared. Seeing the power of his word, the gods rejoiced and proclaimed: Marduk is king! They gave him sceptre, throne and robe and an irresistible weapon.
sections.bodyZh: 众神为马尔杜克设立了一座王者的宝座，他坐在父辈们面前，接受统治的权力。众神对他说：在众神之中，你最受尊崇，你的命运无人可比，你的命令就是安努的命令。从今天起，你的话不可更改，提升和贬低都在你的手中。为了证明他的话有决定命运的力量，众神在中间放了一件衣服，对他说：你开口说“毁灭”，它就会消失；你再开口说“出现”，它就会重新完好如初。马尔杜克一开口，衣服就消失了；他再开口，衣服又出现了。众神看见他的话语如此灵验，都欢喜地向他致敬，喊道：马尔杜克是王！他们把权杖、宝座和王袍交给他，又赐给他一件无敌的武器，让他去击退敌人。

sections.bodyEn: Marduk made a bow and appointed it his weapon, set the arrow and fitted the string; he took the mace in his right hand and hung bow and quiver at his side. He set lightning before him and filled his body with blazing flame. He made a net to enclose Tiamat and stationed the four winds, south, north, east and west, to hold it so she could not escape. He created the evil wind, the whirlwind, the hurricane, the fourfold and sevenfold winds, the tempest and the matchless wind, and they rose behind him. He raised the Flood, his great weapon, and mounted the dreadful storm chariot drawn by four steeds — Killer, Relentless, Trampler and Swift — their teeth full of poison.
sections.bodyZh: 马尔杜克做好了出征的准备：他造了一张弓，把它作为自己的武器，搭上箭，系紧弓弦；他右手拿起权杖，把弓和箭袋挂在身侧。他让闪电走在自己前面，周身充满熊熊的火焰。他又织了一张大网，要把提亚马特网在里面，让南风、北风、东风、西风四方的风抓住网的四角，不让她有一点逃走的余地。他还造出邪风、旋风、飓风、四重风、七重风、狂风和无敌之风，七种风跟在他身后，要搅乱提亚马特的内脏。他举起洪水——他强大的武器，登上令人恐惧、不可抵挡的风暴战车，套上四匹骏马：杀戮者、无情者、践踏者和飞驰者，它们的牙齿里满是毒液。

sections.bodyEn: Marduk went straight towards Tiamat and watched for Qingu's scheme. Seeing him, Qingu faltered and his host was thrown into confusion, but Tiamat did not turn, spitting defiance. Marduk raised the Flood and challenged her: why had she risen in arrogance, set sons against fathers and raised Qingu to a rank not his? Stand forth, you and I, in single combat! Tiamat went mad with rage, shrieked and shook to her roots. They met in battle. Marduk spread his net over her; when she opened her mouth to swallow him, he drove in the evil wind so she could not close her lips. The winds swelled her belly; he shot an arrow that tore her belly, split her inward parts and pierced her heart, and he stood upon her corpse.
sections.bodyZh: 马尔杜克径直走向提亚马特，注视着金古的计谋。金古看见他，脚步乱了，心神不宁，跟随他的众神也都乱了阵脚。提亚马特却毫不回头，嘴里吐着傲慢的话。马尔杜克举起洪水，对她说：你为什么站起来，傲慢地挑起战争？你让子孙背叛父辈，又提升金古做你的丈夫，把不属于他的权力交给他。站出来吧，你和我，单独决斗！提亚马特听了，像疯了一样失去理智，尖声叫喊，浑身从根部颤抖，念起咒语。两人在战场上交锋。马尔杜克撒开大网把她罩住，当她张开嘴想吞下他时，他让邪风灌进她的嘴里，使她无法合拢。狂风充满了她的腹部，她的身体鼓胀，嘴巴大张。马尔杜克射出一箭，箭穿透了她的腹部，劈开了她的内脏，刺穿了她的心。他制服了她，结束了她的生命，把她的尸体扔在地上，站在上面。

sections.bodyEn: When Tiamat was slain, the gods who marched with her broke ranks and fled to save their lives, but they were surrounded with no escape. Marduk bound them and broke their weapons; caught in the net they sat in the snare, filled with lament, and were held in prison. The eleven creatures he led by nose-ropes, bound their arms and trampled them. Qingu too he captured and counted among the dead gods. He took from Qingu the Tablet of Destinies, which was not his by right, sealed it with his seal and fastened it on his own breast.
sections.bodyZh: 提亚马特一死，跟随她的众神四散奔逃，想要保住性命，可是他们被团团围住，无处可逃。马尔杜克把他们捆起来，折断他们的武器，他们被网罗在大网里，坐在陷阱中，充满了悲叹，被关进了牢狱。那十一种怪物，马尔杜克用绳子拴住它们的鼻子，捆住它们的手臂，踩在脚下。金古也被他抓住，被归入死亡之神的行列。马尔杜克从金古身上夺下那块本不属于他的命运泥板，用印章封好，挂在自己的胸前。
sections.headingEn: The captives and the Tablet of Destinies

sections.bodyEn: Marduk returned to Tiamat, crushed her skull with his mace, cut her arteries and let the north wind carry her blood away. He split her like a dried fish into two parts: with one he roofed the sky, drew the bolt and posted guards, ordering them not to let her waters escape. In heaven he set stations for the great gods, fixed their likenesses as constellations, determined the year and its twelve months with three stars each, and made the moon shine, entrusting night to it and teaching it its phases — horns at the month's start, full at mid-month. From the other half he made the earth; from her eyes he opened the Tigris and Euphrates, from her spittle made the clouds, and heaped mountains over her breasts.
sections.bodyZh: 马尔杜克回到提亚马特的身边，用无情的权杖砸碎了她的头骨，割断她的血管，让北风把她的血吹到隐秘的地方。他像劈开一条晒干的鱼一样，把她的身体劈成两半：用一半撑起天空，作为天顶，拉起门闩，安排守卫，命令他们不许让她的水流出来。他又在天上为大神们设立了位置，按照它们的样子安置星座，定下一年的长度，划分出十二个月，每个月三颗星。他让月亮发光，把黑夜托付给它，教它月相的变化：月初生出角来，十五日变圆，然后渐渐亏缺。他用提亚马特的另一半堆成大地，从她的双眼中开出了底格里斯河与幼发拉底河，用她的唾液造出云雾，在她的乳房上堆起高山，开出泉水。
sections.evidenceNote: 《埃努玛·埃利什》第四至五块泥板。
sections.headingEn: Heaven and earth from her body
sections.uncertaintyNote: 第五块泥板长期残缺，后来出土的抄本补足了部分诗行；本站按 eBL 综合文本概述。

sections.bodyEn: The gods asked Marduk to decide their toil. He conceived a marvellous plan and told Ea: I will bring together blood and bone and create a primeval man, 'Man'; let him bear the gods' toil so they may rest. Ea proposed that one god be handed over to make mankind. Marduk asked the assembly who had started the war and incited Tiamat; they answered that it was Qingu. They bound him, brought him before Ea, condemned him and cut his blood vessels, and from his blood Ea created humankind, imposed on it the toil of the gods, and set the gods free. The work, says the poet, was beyond comprehension, done by Ea through Marduk's ingenuity.
sections.bodyZh: 众神请马尔杜克决定他们的劳役。马尔杜克心中想出一个绝妙的计划，对父亲埃阿说：我要把血和骨聚在一起，造出一种原始的人，名叫“人”。让他们来承担众神的劳役，让众神得到休息。埃阿提出：交出一个神来，用他造人。马尔杜克召集众神，问：是谁挑起了这场战争，煽动提亚马特起来造反？众神回答：是金古挑起了战争，煽动提亚马特作乱。他们把金古捆起来，带到埃阿面前，判他有罪，割断了他的血管。埃阿用金古的血造出了人类，把众神的劳役加在人的身上，让众神从此得到自由。诗人说：这件工作超出了人的理解力，是埃阿以马尔杜克的巧思完成的。

sections.bodyEn: The freed Anunnaki offered to build Marduk a shrine where they too might rest. Marduk's face shone like day: build Babylon, he said. The Anunnaki wielded their hoes; for a year they made bricks, and in the second year raised high the head of Esagila and built dwellings for Marduk, Enlil and Ea. At the banquet in the finished temple Anu laid Marduk's bow before the gods, named it and set it in the sky. Then the gods proclaimed Marduk's fifty names, each praising a deed and a power; Enlil gave him his own title Lord of the Lands, and Ea said his name too would be Ea. The poem closes: let these names be kept, let the wise and learned ponder them together, let father tell them to son, so that the land may prosper.
sections.bodyZh: 被解放的阿努纳众神对马尔杜克说：我们要为你建一座圣所，作为你的居所，让我们在其中安歇。马尔杜克听了，脸上像白天一样明亮，说：就建巴比伦吧，那是你们想要的工作。阿努纳众神挥动锄头，第一年做砖，第二年就把埃萨吉拉神庙的顶高高地建起，又为马尔杜克、恩利尔和埃阿建起住所。建成之后，众神在神庙中举行宴会，安努把马尔杜克的弓放在众神面前，为它起了名字，把它安置在天上。然后众神聚在一起，宣告马尔杜克的五十个名字，每一个名字都赞颂他的一种功绩与权能，最后连恩利尔也把自己的名字“万国之主”给了他，埃阿说：他的名字就是埃阿。诗的结尾嘱咐后人：让人们记住这些名字，让智者和学者一起思考，父亲要讲给儿子听，牧人和牧者要侧耳倾听，好让大地丰饶、国家繁荣。

sections.bodyEn: Te Ara writes that in Māori tradition the central act of creation is the separation of earth and sky. The story begins in darkness and nothingness, from which Ranginui the sky father and Papatūānuku the earth mother emerge. At first earth and sky are joined, and their children are born between them.
sections.bodyZh: Te Ara 写道：在毛利传统中，创世的核心行动是天与地的分离。故事从黑暗与虚无开始，天父兰吉努伊与地母帕帕图阿努库从中出现。起初天地紧紧相连，他们的孩子就出生在两者之间。
sections.evidenceNote: Te Ara“毛利创世传统”第1页。

sections.bodyEn: The children decide to separate their parents. Once earth and sky are apart, light enters the world: the move from darkness to light is achieved by the children's act.
sections.bodyZh: 孩子们决定把父母分开。天与地一旦分离，光就照进了世界——从黑暗走向光明，正是由孩子们的这一行动完成的。
sections.uncertaintyNote: Te Ara 说明：在部分部族版本中，塔内在分开天地时起重要作用；本站不选定某一部族的说法。

sections.bodyEn: After the separation the children become atua of different parts of nature: Tāne of the forests, Tangaroa of the sea, Rūaumoko of earthquakes, Tāwhirimātea of winds and weather. Weaving these atua into one genealogy is the traditional Māori way of explaining the natural world.
sections.bodyZh: 分离之后，孩子们成为自然各部分的神（atua）：塔内是森林之神，塔加罗阿是海洋之神，还有地震之神鲁奥莫科、风与天气之神塔维里马特阿。把这些神编进同一个谱系，是毛利人解释自然世界的传统方式。
sections.uncertaintyNote: 鲁奥莫科与塔维里马特阿尚未建立独立实体。

sections.bodyEn: Te Ara also cautions that tribal versions vary considerably, especially on the role of a supreme being. This retelling covers only the common threads the public page summarizes; named iwi versions require permission from the appropriate authority.
sections.bodyZh: Te Ara 也提醒，各部族的创世故事差异很大，特别是关于至高存在的角色。这里只讲公开页面所总结的共同线索，具名部族的版本须经相应权威授权。
sections.uncertaintyNote: 具名 iwi／hapū 版本仍为权限阻塞。

stories.canonicalTitle: Nüwa repairs the sky — Huainanzi and Liezi witnesses

conflicts.claimAStatement: In the Liezi Tang Wen witness the Gonggong episode is introduced with 其後 after Nüwa's repair.
conflicts.claimBStatement: The Huainanzi Tian Wen witness narrates the Gonggong collision on its own as an explanation of cosmic orientation without naming Nüwa.
conflicts.resolutionNotes: Keep both placements. Do not adopt the later retelling in which the collision causes the repair until that reception layer is registered with exact locators.
conflicts.storyNotes: The Liezi witness attaches Gonggong after the repair; no causal synthesis.
conflicts.summary: Liezi Tang Wen places the Gonggong collision after Nüwa's repair, while Huainanzi Tian Wen narrates it as a standalone cosmological etiology without Nüwa.

stories.editorialNote: 两份传世文献逐段并列；《列子》传世本成书年代有争议，不据此排序。后世因果化的复述作为独立接受层排队。
stories.summaryEn: Huainanzi “Lan Ming” and Liezi “Tang Wen” both have Nüwa refine five-colored stones and cut a turtle's legs to set up the four poles; the former adds the black dragon and reed ash, while the latter frames the repair as a remedy for deficient things and introduces Gonggong only afterwards. The two witnesses are read separately and are not merged into the later version in which Gonggong's collision causes the repair.
stories.summaryZh: 《淮南子·览冥训》与《列子·汤问》都记载女娲炼五色石、断鳌足立四极；前者另有黑龙与芦灰，后者把补天放在天地“物有不足”的问答里，并在其后才引出共工。两份见证分开阅读，不合成后世“共工撞山导致女娲补天”的版本。
stories.titleZh: 女娲补天：《淮南子》与《列子》两种见证

sections.bodyEn: Huainanzi “Lan Ming” sets the scene in remote antiquity: the four poles holding up the world have failed and the nine provinces have split; heaven no longer covers everything and earth no longer bears everything, fires and floods cannot be stopped, and wild beasts and birds of prey attack the people. This section follows only this witness and adds no cause taken from other texts.
sections.bodyZh: 《淮南子·览冥训》以远古为背景：支撑天地的四极崩坏，九州开裂，天不能全覆、地不能全载，大火与洪水都无法止息，猛兽鸷鸟危害百姓。本段只按这一见证的顺序概述，不补入其他文献给出的起因。
sections.evidenceNote: 《淮南子·览冥训》“往古之时”段；Chinese Text Project 章节页。
sections.uncertaintyNote: 传世本用字存在异体；本站只发布独立概述，不复制整段原文。

sections.bodyEn: Nüwa then refines five-colored stones to patch the azure sky and cuts off the legs of a great turtle to set the four poles upright again.
sections.bodyZh: 于是女娲炼五色石来修补苍天，又截断巨鳌的足，用来重新立起四极。
sections.evidenceNote: 同段女娲补天与立四极的句组。
sections.headingEn: Five-colored stones and the turtle's legs
sections.uncertaintyNote: 炼字与鳌字在不同版本中有异体，不影响本段概述。

sections.bodyEn: This witness adds that Nüwa kills a black dragon to relieve Jizhou and piles up reed ash to stop the flood waters; afterwards heaven and earth are set right and the people survive.
sections.bodyZh: 这一见证还写到女娲杀死黑龙以救济冀州，并堆积芦苇灰来堵住泛滥的洪水；随后天地重新安定，百姓得以存活。
sections.evidenceNote: 同段黑龙、冀州与芦灰句组。
sections.headingEn: The black dragon and the reed ash
sections.uncertaintyNote: 冀州在此是文本中的九州之一，不映射为现代行政区或坐标；《列子·汤问》对应段落未陈述这两项。

sections.bodyEn: The Lan Ming Nüwa passage does not attribute the collapse to Gonggong. The Huainanzi does narrate Gonggong striking Mount Buzhou, but in a separate passage in the “Tian Wen” chapter that explains the tilt of heaven and earth; the site does not splice the two chapters into a causal chain.
sections.bodyZh: 《览冥训》的女娲段落没有把天地崩坏归因于共工。《淮南子》确实在《天文训》另记共工怒触不周山，但那是另一章中独立的天地倾斜起源，本站不把两章拼接成因果链。
sections.evidenceNote: 《览冥训》女娲段与《天文训》共工段分别定位。

claims.statement: The Tang Wen Nüwa–Gonggong passage is a scoped part of the Liezi.
The Liezi Tang Wen passage is a textual witness of Nüwa repairing the sky.
The popular sequence in which Gonggong's collision causes Nüwa's repair is not back-projected into the Huainanzi or Liezi witnesses and is queued as a later reception layer.
Both registered witnesses use the collision to explain why heaven tilts northwest and waters flow to the southeast.
Both registered witnesses say that the great turtle's legs are cut off to set up the four poles.
The Liezi Tang Wen witness frames the repair inside a dialogue on whether heaven and earth, as things, have deficiencies.
Nüwa refines five-colored stones to repair the sky in both registered witnesses.
Nüwa is the actor who repairs the sky in both registered witnesses.
In the Liezi Tang Wen witness the Gonggong episode is introduced with 其後 after Nüwa's repair.

entities.notes: Actor of the repair; designation 女媧氏.
Legs set up as the four poles.

sections.bodyEn: Liezi “Tang Wen” places the repair inside a dialogue between Tang of Yin and Xia Ge on whether heaven and earth have limits: heaven and earth are also things, things have deficiencies, and so in antiquity Nüwa mended the gap.
sections.bodyZh: 《列子·汤问》把女娲补天放在殷汤与夏革关于天地有无极限的问答中：天地也是物，物都有不足之处，所以古时女娲修补了它的缺口。
sections.evidenceNote: 《列子·汤问》殷汤与夏革问答段。
sections.headingEn: Heaven and earth are also things
sections.uncertaintyNote: 《列子》托名列御寇，传世本成书年代有争议；本站不据此把它排在《淮南子》之前。

sections.bodyEn: This witness likewise has Nüwa refine five-colored stones to fill the gap and cut the turtle's legs to set up the four poles; it does not mention the black dragon, Jizhou or reed ash.
sections.bodyZh: 这一见证同样写女娲炼五色石补其缺口，并截断鳌足以立四极；它没有写黑龙、冀州或芦灰。
sections.headingEn: Five-colored stones and the turtle's legs
sections.uncertaintyNote: “未陈述”只描述本段范围，不是对《淮南子》细节的否定。

sections.bodyEn: Right after the repair, “Tang Wen” uses “afterwards” to introduce Gonggong contending with Zhuanxu for rulership and striking Mount Buzhou in anger. In this witness the Gonggong episode follows Nüwa's repair; it is not its cause.
sections.bodyZh: 紧接补天之后，《汤问》用“其后”引出共工氏与颛顼争为帝、怒触不周之山。在这一见证里，共工事件发生在女娲补天之后，而不是它的起因。
sections.uncertaintyNote: 后世“共工触山导致女娲补天”的因果顺序不回写进本见证。

sections.bodyEn: Gonggong's blow breaks the pillar of heaven and snaps the cords of the earth, so heaven tilts toward the northwest, where the sun, moon and stars move, and the earth falls short in the southeast, where the rivers and flood waters gather.
sections.bodyZh: 共工撞山折断天柱、断绝地维，于是天向西北倾斜，日月星辰向那里移动；地在东南不满，众水因此流归东南。
sections.headingEn: Heaven tilts northwest, waters gather southeast
sections.uncertaintyNote: 这是文本中的天地形势起源解释，不作为地理或天文史实。

stories.canonicalTitle: Gonggong strikes Mount Buzhou — two early witnesses

conflicts.claimAStatement: In the Liezi Tang Wen witness the Gonggong episode is introduced with 其後 after Nüwa's repair.
conflicts.claimBStatement: The Huainanzi Tian Wen witness narrates the Gonggong collision on its own as an explanation of cosmic orientation without naming Nüwa.
conflicts.resolutionNotes: Keep both placements. Do not adopt the later retelling in which the collision causes the repair until that reception layer is registered with exact locators.
conflicts.storyNotes: Standalone etiology versus sequel to Nüwa's repair.
conflicts.summary: Liezi Tang Wen places the Gonggong collision after Nüwa's repair, while Huainanzi Tian Wen narrates it as a standalone cosmological etiology without Nüwa.

stories.summaryEn: Huainanzi “Tian Wen” narrates Gonggong contending with Zhuanxu and striking Mount Buzhou as a standalone explanation of why heaven and earth tilt; Liezi “Tang Wen” attaches the same event after Nüwa's repair with “afterwards”. Neither witness makes it the cause of Nüwa's repair.

stories.canonicalTitle: Churning of the Ocean — Mahābhārata critical edition and Bhāgavata Purāṇa witnesses

conflicts.claimAStatement: In the Mahābhārata critical-edition witness the tortoise king Akūpāra bears Mount Mandara during the churning.
conflicts.claimBStatement: In the Bhāgavata Purāṇa witness Viṣṇu, in the form of a giant tortoise, raises Mount Mandara on his back.
conflicts.resolutionNotes: Retain both as coexisting textual witnesses. Akūpāra and Kūrma remain separate entities; no identity claim is made without an explicit source-backed identification.
conflicts.storyNotes: v0.30 witness comparison; Akūpāra and Kūrma are not equated.
conflicts.summary: The Mahābhārata critical edition (Ādiparvan 1.16) has the tortoise king Akūpāra bear Mount Mandara, while the Bhāgavata Purāṇa (8.7) has Viṣṇu himself assume a tortoise form to raise it.

stories.editorialNote: 精校本正文与往世书分开对读；“未陈述”不等于所有写本都没有。现代虔信译本不复制，神学解释不作裁定。
stories.summaryEn: Both Sanskrit witnesses use Mount Mandara as the rod and Vāsuki as the rope, have Dhanvantari emerge with the amṛta and Rāhu beheaded by the discus; but the tortoise supporting the mountain is the tortoise king Akūpāra in the critical edition and Viṣṇu's tortoise form in the Bhāgavata Purāṇa, and Śiva drinking the poison appears only at the latter's locator. The Angkor Wat relief remains a separate material witness.
stories.summaryZh: 两份梵语见证都以曼陀罗山为搅棒、婆苏吉为搅绳，并让檀文陀利捧着甘露出现、罗睺被神盘斩首；但托山的龟在精校本中是龟王阿库帕拉，在《薄伽梵往世书》中是毗湿奴的龟形化身，湿婆饮毒也只见于后者的当前定位。吴哥寺浮雕继续作为独立的物质见证。
stories.titleZh: 乳海搅拌：《摩诃婆罗多》精校本与《薄伽梵往世书》

claims.statement: The churning passage witness is part of the Ādiparvan of the Mahābhārata.

sections.bodyEn: In the critical edition at Ādiparvan 1.15, the gods gather on Mount Meru to deliberate how to obtain the amṛta; Nārāyaṇa (Viṣṇu) advises that gods and asuras churn the ocean together.
sections.bodyZh: 精校本《初篇》1.15 中，诸神聚集在须弥山上商议如何得到甘露；那罗延（毗湿奴）建议诸神与阿修罗一起搅动大海。
sections.uncertaintyNote: “那罗延”在此按既有毗湿奴实体连接，不扩展神学解释。

sections.bodyEn: The serpent Ananta uproots Mount Mandara to serve as the churning rod and the nāga Vāsuki serves as the rope; the tortoise king Akūpāra bears the base of the mountain. This witness does not say that the tortoise king is a form of Viṣṇu.
sections.bodyZh: 巨蛇阿难陀拔起曼陀罗山作为搅棒，龙王婆苏吉充当搅绳；山的底部由龟王阿库帕拉承托。这一见证没有说龟王是毗湿奴的化身。
sections.headingEn: Mandara, Vāsuki and the tortoise king
sections.headingZh: 曼陀罗山、婆苏吉与龟王
sections.uncertaintyNote: 阿难陀拔山一项为中等置信度，待逐颂校对；阿难陀尚未单独建实体。

sections.bodyEn: As the churning goes on, a series of beings and treasures emerges, and finally Dhanvantari appears holding a vessel filled with the amṛta.
sections.bodyZh: 搅拌中先后涌现多种存在与宝物，最后檀文陀利捧着盛满甘露的水罐出现。
sections.headingZh: 檀文陀利捧着甘露出现
sections.uncertaintyNote: 此前出现之物的逐项清单尚未建模，不从其他版本补齐。

sections.bodyEn: After the Dānavas seize the amṛta, Nārāyaṇa takes on a deluding female form and recovers it for the gods. Rāhu, disguised as a god, drinks some of it; when the Sun and Moon expose him, Nārāyaṇa cuts off his head with the discus, and a great battle between gods and Dānavas follows.
sections.bodyZh: 阿修罗夺走甘露后，那罗延化作迷惑人的女子形象，把甘露取回交给诸神。罗睺假扮天神偷饮甘露，被日月揭发后，那罗延以神盘斩下其头；随后天神与阿修罗爆发大战。
sections.headingEn: The deluding female form and Rāhu
sections.uncertaintyNote: 专名实体“摩希尼”只连接《薄伽梵往世书》见证；此处保留“迷惑的女身”描述。

sections.bodyEn: In Bhāgavata Purāṇa 8.5–8.6, on Viṣṇu's advice the gods make a temporary truce with the asuras; together they uproot Mount Mandara and carry it toward the ocean, with Viṣṇu himself stepping in to help.
sections.bodyZh: 《薄伽梵往世书》第八篇第5–6章中，诸神按毗湿奴的建议与阿修罗暂时结盟，合力拔起曼陀罗山并运往大海，毗湿奴亲自出手相助。

sections.headingZh: 诸神与阿修罗暂时结盟
sections.uncertaintyNote: 运山过程的细节只作概述，待逐颂校对。

sections.bodyEn: Once the churning begins with Vāsuki as the rope, Mount Mandara sinks into the water; Viṣṇu assumes the form of a giant tortoise, dives beneath it and raises the mountain on his back.
sections.bodyZh: 以婆苏吉为绳开始搅拌后，曼陀罗山沉入水中；毗湿奴化作巨龟潜到山下，用背托起大山。

sections.bodyEn: The churning first produces a terrible poison that spreads in every direction; beings turn to Śiva, who drinks it.
sections.bodyZh: 搅拌最先产生可怕的毒药，向各方蔓延；众生求助于湿婆，湿婆把毒药饮下。
sections.uncertaintyNote: 后续图像传统与虔信解释未在本批次逐句建模。

sections.bodyEn: A series of treasures and beings then emerges, and finally Dhanvantari appears holding a vessel filled with the amṛta.
sections.bodyZh: 其后又涌现多种宝物与存在，最后檀文陀利捧着盛满甘露的水罐出现。
sections.uncertaintyNote: 此前出现之物的逐项清单尚未建模，不与精校本合并。

sections.bodyEn: When the asuras snatch the amṛta, Viṣṇu becomes Mohinī, captivates them and distributes the amṛta to the gods. Rāhu, disguised as a god, slips in and drinks; when the Sun and Moon point him out, Viṣṇu severs his head with the discus.
sections.bodyZh: 阿修罗抢走甘露后，毗湿奴化身为摩希尼迷惑他们，并把甘露分给诸神。罗睺假扮天神混入其中饮下甘露，被日月指认后，毗湿奴以神盘斩下其头。
sections.uncertaintyNote: 罗睺后来的天体身份不在本批次建模。

stories.canonicalTitle: From Atum to Horus — a family of Egyptian gods
stories.editorialNote: 学术综述层；古代文本见证尚未逐条拆分，各神亲属关系以 UCL 页面的表述为准。
stories.summaryEn: UCL Digital Egypt orders scattered ancient references into one divine family: the sun-god Atum brings forth Shu and Tefnet, who produce Geb (earth) and Nut (sky); Shu holds them apart. Later Seth murders his brother Osiris, and Isis gathers the body and conceives Horus. It is a scholarly synthesis, not the sequence of a single ancient text.
stories.summaryZh: UCL 数字埃及把零散的古代文献整理成一个神族谱系：太阳神阿图姆生出舒与泰芙努特，他们又生出大地之神盖布与天空女神努特；舒把天地分开。后来塞特杀害兄弟奥西里斯，伊西斯收集遗体并怀上荷鲁斯。这是一份学术综述，不是某一部古代文献的原文顺序。
stories.titleZh: 从阿图姆到荷鲁斯：埃及众神的一家

sections.bodyEn: In Egyptian creation thought the principal creator is the sun-god, also called Atum. His first offshoots are a son and a daughter, Shu and Tefnet; scholars link Shu's name to dryness and read Tefnet as moisture.
sections.bodyZh: 在埃及的创世观念里，主要的创造者是太阳神，他也被称为阿图姆。他最先生出一男一女：舒和泰芙努特。学者认为“舒”这个名字和“干燥”有关，“泰芙努特”则代表湿润。

sections.uncertaintyNote: “干燥／湿润”是现代学者的词源解释。

sections.bodyEn: Shu and Tefnet in turn produce two children: Geb, god of the earth, and Nut, goddess of the sky — dryness and moisture crystallised into solid earth and a sky the Egyptians thought of as watery.
sections.bodyZh: 舒和泰芙努特又生下两个孩子：大地之神盖布和天空女神努特。干燥与湿润，变成了坚实的大地和古埃及人眼中充满水的天空。

sections.bodyEn: Shu separates Geb and Nut, sky above and earth below. Scattered references suggest the separation had to be enforced, or earth and sky would keep producing divine offspring.
sections.bodyZh: 盖布和努特被舒分开，天在上、地在下。零散的古代记载暗示，这种分离必须被强制维持，否则天地还会继续生出神来。

sections.bodyEn: Later Osiris's anarchic brother Seth, out of jealousy, murders him, dismembers him and takes his place as king of the world. Isis collects the limbs and revives the body enough to conceive a child, Horus.
sections.bodyZh: 后来，奥西里斯“无序的兄弟”塞特出于嫉妒杀害了他，把遗体分开，并取代他成为世界之王。伊西斯找回奥西里斯的肢体，让遗体恢复到足以受孕，生下了荷鲁斯。

stories.canonicalTitle: Izanagi and Izanami — making the land, Yomi and purification
stories.editorialNote: 依据张伯伦 1882 年英译《古事记》的第三至第十节；《日本书纪》的不同说法另行保存，不合并。
stories.summaryEn: The heavenly deities command Izanagi and Izanami to consolidate the drifting land. From the Floating Bridge of Heaven they stir the brine with a jewelled spear, and the drops become Onogoro Island. Izanami dies after bearing the fire deity; Izanagi follows her to Yomi, but she has already eaten of its hearth. Returning, he purifies himself, and from his left eye, right eye and nose are born Amaterasu, Tsukuyomi and Susanoo.
stories.summaryZh: 天神命伊邪那岐与伊邪那美巩固漂浮的大地。两神站在天浮桥上，用天沼矛搅动海水，滴下的盐水堆成淤能碁吕岛。伊邪那美生下火神后被烧伤而死；伊邪那岐追到黄泉，她却说已经吃了黄泉的食物。伊邪那岐回来后洗净身体，最后从左眼、右眼和鼻子生出天照大神、月读和须佐之男。
stories.titleZh: 伊邪那岐与伊邪那美：造岛、黄泉与禊祓

sections.headingEn: The birth of the fire deity

sections.bodyEn: Longing to see her, Izanagi follows Izanami to Yomi and asks her to come back, for the lands they made are not yet finished. She answers that he has come too late: she has already eaten from the hearth of Yomi — yet she agrees to consult the deities there.
sections.bodyZh: 伊邪那岐想再见到妻子，便追到黄泉，请她回去：“我们造的国土还没有完成。”伊邪那美回答：你来得太晚了，我已经吃了黄泉灶火煮的东西——不过她答应去和黄泉的神商量。
sections.uncertaintyNote: 之后的逃离情节可参看本库“黄泉中的八雷神”故事。

sections.bodyEn: Back from Yomi, Izanagi bathes to purify himself, and deities are born as he washes. Last of all, washing his left eye brings forth Amaterasu, his right eye Tsukuyomi, and his nose Susanoo.
sections.bodyZh: 伊邪那岐回来后在水中洗净自己，身上不断化生出神。最后，他洗左眼时生出天照大神，洗右眼时生出月读，洗鼻子时生出须佐之男。
sections.evidenceNote: 张伯伦译本第十节（kj017）及译注。
sections.uncertaintyNote: 三神的通行名称来自译者注释。

stories.canonicalTitle: Njörðr, Freyr and Freyja — the Vanir family
stories.editorialNote: 依据《欺骗古鲁菲》第23、24、37章；诗体埃达中的对应诗篇另行登记。
stories.summaryEn: Njörðr lives at Nóatún and rules wind and sea; raised in Vanaheim, he came to the Æsir as a hostage. His son Freyr rules rain, sunshine and harvests; his daughter Freyja lives at Fólkvangr, takes half the slain and drives a chariot pulled by two cats. Later Freyr gives away his sword to win Gerðr.
stories.summaryZh: 尼奥尔德住在诺欧通，掌管风和海，原本在华纳海姆长大，作为人质来到阿萨神族。他的儿子弗雷掌管雨水、阳光和丰收；女儿芙蕾雅住在弗尔克范格，每次出征都分走一半战死者，乘坐两只猫拉的车。弗雷后来为了娶葛德，交出了自己的宝剑。
stories.titleZh: 华纳神族：尼奥尔德、弗雷与芙蕾雅

claims.statement: Freyja's dwelling is Fólkvangr.
Njörðr lives in heaven at the place called Nóatún.
Njörðr was brought up in Vanaheim and given to the Æsir as a hostage.
Freyja drives a chariot drawn by two cats.
Whenever Freyja rides to battle she gets half the slain, and Odin the other half.
Freyr rules rain and sunshine and the produce of the earth, and is invoked for prosperity.
To win Gerðr, Freyr gives away his sword.
Njörðr rules the motion of the wind, calms sea and fire, and is invoked for voyages and fishing.
Njörðr's daughter is Freyja.
Njörðr's son is Freyr.
Freyr and Freyja are the children of Njörðr.

events.summaryEn: Njörðr lives in heaven at a place called Nóatún.

sections.bodyEn: Njörðr lives in heaven at a place called Nóatún. He rules the motion of the wind and can calm sea and fire; those who sail or fish pray to him. He was raised in Vanaheim and later given to the Æsir as a hostage.
sections.bodyZh: 尼奥尔德住在天上一个叫诺欧通的地方。他掌管风的运行，能平息海浪和火焰；出海航行和捕鱼的人都向他祈祷。他在华纳海姆长大，后来作为人质被送到阿萨神族。

sections.bodyEn: Njörðr has a son and a daughter. Freyr rules rain, sunshine and the produce of the earth, and people pray to him for good seasons and wealth. Freyja lives at Fólkvangr; whenever she rides to battle she takes half the slain, Odin the other half, and her chariot is drawn by two cats.
sections.bodyZh: 尼奥尔德有一儿一女。儿子弗雷掌管雨水、阳光和大地的收成，人们向他祈求丰年与富足。女儿芙蕾雅住在弗尔克范格，每当她骑马出战，就分得一半战死者，另一半归奥丁；她乘坐的车由两只猫拉着。

sections.bodyEn: Later Freyr falls in love with Gerðr, a giant's daughter. To win her he gives away his sword as the price, and the sword is no longer his.
sections.bodyZh: 后来，弗雷爱上了巨人之女葛德。为了娶到她，他把自己的宝剑交给了别人作为代价——这把剑从此不在他手中。
sections.uncertaintyNote: 葛德尚未单独建立实体；诸神黄昏中的后果另行登记。

stories.canonicalTitle: Týr's hand and the binding of Fenrir
stories.editorialNote: 依据《欺骗古鲁菲》第25、34章；芬里尔在诸神黄昏中的结局见既有故事。
stories.summaryEn: Týr is the boldest of the gods. When they set out to bind the growing wolf Fenrir, the wolf demands a hand in its mouth as a pledge. Only Týr offers his right hand; when the wolf finds it cannot break free, it bites the hand off — and so Týr is one-handed.
stories.summaryZh: 提尔是众神中最勇敢的一位。众神要捆住越长越大的狼芬里尔，狼要求有人把手放进它嘴里作担保。只有提尔伸出了右手；当狼发现自己挣脱不开，就咬断了他的手。所以提尔只有一只手。
stories.titleZh: 提尔的手：束缚芬里尔

claims.statement: Fenrir is the wolf bound by the gods.
Týr is the boldest and most valiant of the gods, and he is one-handed.
As a pledge while the wolf is bound, Týr puts his right hand in Fenrir's mouth; when the wolf is not released it bites the hand off.

events.summaryEn: Snorri says Týr is the boldest and most valiant of the gods, invoked for victory in battle — and he has only one hand.
events.summaryZh: 斯诺里说，提尔是众神中最勇敢、最无畏的一位，打仗时人们向他祈求胜利。

events.summaryEn: The gods mean to bind the wolf Fenrir with a magic fetter.
events.summaryZh: 众神想用一条魔法绳索捆住狼芬里尔。

events.summaryEn: The more the wolf struggles, the tighter the fetter grows.
events.summaryZh: 绳索越挣越紧，狼发现自己被骗了，便咬断了提尔的手。

sections.bodyEn: The gods mean to bind the wolf Fenrir with a magic fetter. Suspicious, the wolf demands that someone put a hand in its mouth as a pledge of good faith. Only Týr holds out his right hand.
sections.bodyZh: 众神想用一条魔法绳索捆住狼芬里尔。狼起了疑心，要求有人把手放进它嘴里，保证这不是诡计。众神面面相觑，只有提尔伸出了右手。

sections.bodyEn: The more the wolf struggles, the tighter the fetter grows. Realizing it has been tricked, Fenrir bites off Týr's hand — and all the gods laugh, except Týr.
sections.bodyZh: 绳索越挣越紧，狼发现自己被骗了，便咬断了提尔的手。众神都笑了，只有提尔没有笑。

stories.canonicalTitle: Heimdallr, watchman of the gods
stories.editorialNote: 依据《欺骗古鲁菲》第27章。
stories.summaryEn: Heimdallr lives at Himinbjörg beside the rainbow bridge Bifröst and guards it for the gods against the mountain-giants. He needs less sleep than a bird, sees a hundred leagues by night, and hears grass and wool growing. His horn Gjallarhorn can be heard in all worlds, and he is called the son of nine mothers who were sisters.
stories.summaryZh: 海姆达尔住在彩虹桥边的希敏约格，替众神守着桥，防备山巨人。他睡得比鸟还少，夜里能看见一百里远，连草和羊毛生长的声音都听得见。他有一支加拉尔号角，吹响时所有世界都能听到。人们还说他是九位姐妹母亲的儿子。
stories.titleZh: 海姆达尔：众神的守望者

stories.canonicalTitle: Ymir and the shaping of the world
stories.editorialNote: 依据《欺骗古鲁菲》第5–8章；《女巫的预言》等诗歌见证另行对读。
stories.summaryEn: In the beginning there is a great void where rime from the north meets heat from the south, and from it the giant Ymir arises. Later Odin and his brothers Vili and Vé kill Ymir and build the world from his body: his flesh becomes the earth, his blood the sea and lakes, his bones the rocks, his skull the sky.
stories.summaryZh: 太初有一道深渊，北方的寒霜遇到南方的热气，化出巨人尤弥尔。后来奥丁和他的兄弟维利、维杀死了尤弥尔，用他的身体造出世界：肉成了大地，血成了海洋和湖泊，骨头成了山石，头骨成了天空。
stories.titleZh: 尤弥尔与世界的形成

Ymir arises in Ginnungagap where rime from the north meets heat from the south.
From Ymir's flesh the earth is made, from his blood the sea and lakes, from his bones the rocks, and from his skull the sky.
Odin and his brothers shape the world from Ymir's body.
Ymir's body becomes the material of the world.

stories.canonicalTitle: Frigg's oaths and the death of Baldr
stories.editorialNote: 依据《欺骗古鲁菲》第20、49章；之后的冥界求情与报复情节尚未逐段登记。
stories.summaryEn: Frigg, Odin's wife, knows all fates. When her son Baldr dreams of danger, she makes fire, water, metals, stones, plants and beasts swear not to harm him — all except a young shoot of mistletoe. In the end it is mistletoe that kills Baldr.
stories.summaryZh: 弗丽嘉是奥丁的妻子，知道一切命运。她的儿子巴德尔梦见自己有危险，她便让火、水、金属、石头、草木和野兽都发誓不伤害他——唯独漏掉了一株幼小的槲寄生。巴德尔最后正是被槲寄生杀死的。
stories.titleZh: 弗丽嘉的誓言与巴德尔之死

claims.statement: Baldr dreams ominous dreams threatening his life, and the Æsir resolve to secure protection for him against every danger.
Frigg takes oaths from fire, water, metals, stones, earth, trees, sicknesses, beasts, birds, poisons and snakes not to harm Baldr.
Disguised as a woman, Loki learns from Frigg that the young mistletoe west of Valhöll swore no oath, and pulls it up.
Guided by Loki, the blind Höðr throws the mistletoe, which pierces Baldr and kills him.
Odin bears Baldr's death most heavily of all the gods, understanding best what a loss it is for the Æsir.
At Frigg's request Hermóðr the Bold, Odin's son, mounts Sleipnir and rides to Hel to ransom Baldr.
At Baldr's ship-funeral his wife Nanna dies of grief and is burned beside him, while Odin lays the ring Draupnir on the pyre.
Hermóðr rides nine nights through dark valleys to the Gjallarbrú, where the maiden Móðguðr tells him the road to Hel lies downward and north.
Hel agrees to release Baldr only if all things in the world, living and dead, weep for him; if any refuses, he stays.
The Æsir send messengers through the world, and men, beasts, earth, stones, trees and metals all weep for Baldr.
A giantess named Þökk, believed to be Loki, alone refuses to weep for Baldr, so he remains in Hel.
When Loki, as a salmon, tries to leap over the gods' net in the Fránangr falls, Thor catches him by the tail.
With Loki bound by his son's entrails beneath Skaði's serpent, Sigyn holds a bowl to catch the venom; when she empties it, his writhing causes earthquakes.

events.summaryEn: Baldr, Odin's son, is the best of the gods and all praise him; so fair and bright that the whitest flower is called Baldr's brow.
events.summaryZh: 奥丁的儿子巴德尔是众神中最好的一位，人人都称赞他。

events.summaryEn: Frigg took oaths that they would not harm Baldr from fire and water, iron and every metal, stones, the earth, trees, sicknesses, beasts, birds, poison and snakes.
events.summaryZh: 于是弗丽嘉出发，让世间万物都立下誓言，不伤害巴德尔：火与水、铁和各种金属、石头、泥土、树木、疾病、走兽、飞鸟、毒物和蛇，全都发了誓。

events.summaryEn: Loki Laufeyjarson was displeased that Baldr took no harm.
events.summaryZh: 劳菲之子洛基看见这一切，心里很不高兴，因为巴德尔毫发无伤。

events.summaryEn: Höðr stood at the edge of the ring, for he was blind.
events.summaryZh: 霍德尔站在人圈的外面，因为他是瞎子。

events.summaryEn: When Baldr fell, the Æsir were struck dumb and their hands failed them to lift him.
events.summaryZh: 巴德尔倒下的时候，阿萨众神都说不出话来，双手也失去了力气，不能把他扶起。

events.summaryEn: When the gods came to themselves, Frigg asked who among the Æsir would win all her love and favour by riding the road to Hel to find Baldr and offer Hel a ransom to let him come home to Ásgarðr.
events.summaryZh: 众神稍稍平静之后，弗丽嘉开口问道：阿萨神族中有谁愿意赢得我全部的爱与恩宠，骑马走上通往冥界的路，去找赫尔，问她要多少赎金才肯让巴德尔回到阿斯加德？

events.summaryEn: The Æsir carried Baldr's body to the sea.
events.summaryZh: 阿萨众神抬起巴德尔的尸体，送到海边。

events.summaryEn: For nine nights Hermóðr rode through dark, deep valleys where he could see nothing, until he came to the river Gjöll and rode onto the Gjallarbrú, roofed with gleaming gold.
events.summaryZh: 赫尔莫德骑着马走了九天九夜，穿过幽深黑暗的山谷，什么也看不见，直到来到冥河耶尔河边，骑上了铺着闪亮黄金的耶尔桥。

events.summaryEn: At Hel's gate Hermóðr dismounted, tightened the girth, remounted and spurred Sleipnir, who leapt clean over the gate.
events.summaryZh: 赫尔莫德一路骑到冥界的大门前，他跳下马，把马肚带勒紧，重新上马，用马刺一踢，骏马高高跃起，从大门上方越了过去，一点也没碰到。

events.summaryEn: Hermóðr rode back and told all he had seen and heard.
events.summaryZh: 赫尔莫德骑马回到阿斯加德，把他的所见所闻原原本本地告诉了众神。

events.summaryEn: As the messengers were returning, having done their errand well, they found a giantess sitting in a cave who called herself Þökk.
events.summaryZh: 使者们完成了使命，正在回家的路上，看见一个山洞里坐着一个女巨人，她自称叫作索克。
events.titleEn: The giantess who would not weep
events.uncertaintyNote: 斯诺里说“人们认为”索克就是洛基，这是传统中的认定，不是故事中直接揭穿的情节。

events.summaryEn: The gods were so angry that Loki fled and built a house with four doors on a mountain so he could watch every way, and by day he often hid as a salmon in the Fránangr falls.
events.summaryZh: 众神对洛基怒不可遏，洛基逃到一座山上，盖了一间有四扇门的房子，好向四面八方都能看见。

events.summaryEn: The gods took Loki into a cave, set up three slabs on edge and bored a hole in each.
events.summaryZh: 众神把洛基带进一个山洞，竖起三块扁石，在每块石头上钻一个洞。

sections.bodyEn: Baldr, Odin's son, is the best of the gods and all praise him; so fair and bright that the whitest flower is called Baldr's brow. He is the wisest, most eloquent and most merciful of the Æsir, though none of his judgements can be fulfilled. Then Baldr dreamed great and perilous dreams threatening his life, and when he told the Æsir they took counsel together and resolved to ask protection for him from every kind of danger.
sections.bodyZh: 奥丁的儿子巴德尔是众神中最好的一位，人人都称赞他。他容貌俊美、光彩照人，有一种最白的花就因为像他的睫毛那样白，被人们称作“巴德尔的睫毛”。他是阿萨神族中最聪明、最善于言辞、最仁慈的神，可是他的判决却从来不能实现。这一天，巴德尔做了几个可怕的梦，梦见自己的性命将要遭到危险。他把这些梦告诉了阿萨众神，众神聚在一起商议，最后决定：要为巴德尔求得一切东西的保护，使他免受任何伤害。

sections.bodyEn: Frigg took oaths that they would not harm Baldr from fire and water, iron and every metal, stones, the earth, trees, sicknesses, beasts, birds, poison and snakes. When this was done it became a sport of the Æsir: Baldr would stand in the assembly while some shot at him, some struck at him and some threw stones, and nothing harmed him. They all thought it a great honour.
sections.bodyZh: 于是弗丽嘉出发，让世间万物都立下誓言，不伤害巴德尔：火与水、铁和各种金属、石头、泥土、树木、疾病、走兽、飞鸟、毒物和蛇，全都发了誓。这件事办成之后，众神都放下心来，并且以此为乐：巴德尔站在集会的场地中央，其他的神有的向他射箭，有的用刀剑砍他，有的向他扔石头，可是无论做什么都伤不了他。众神都认为这是一件了不起的荣耀。

sections.bodyEn: Loki Laufeyjarson was displeased that Baldr took no harm. He went to Frigg at Fensalir in the likeness of a woman. Frigg told the stranger that neither weapons nor trees would harm Baldr, for she had taken oaths of all things. Had everything sworn? asked the woman. Frigg answered that a young shoot grew west of Valhöll called mistletoe, which seemed too young to ask for an oath. The woman went away; Loki took the mistletoe, pulled it up and went to the assembly.
sections.bodyZh: 劳菲之子洛基看见这一切，心里很不高兴，因为巴德尔毫发无伤。他变成一个女人，来到弗丽嘉住的芬萨利尔宫。弗丽嘉问这位女子：你知道阿萨众神在集会上做什么吗？女人说：他们都在朝巴德尔射箭、扔东西，可是什么也伤不了他。弗丽嘉说：不论是兵器还是木头，都伤不了巴德尔，因为我已经让万物都立了誓。女人问：真的万物都向你发誓不伤害巴德尔了吗？弗丽嘉答道：在瓦尔哈拉的西边，长着一棵小小的树苗，叫作槲寄生。我觉得它太年幼了，就没有让它发誓。那女人听了便走了。洛基找到槲寄生，把它拔下来，带到集会的地方去。

sections.bodyEn: Höðr stood at the edge of the ring, for he was blind. Loki asked why he did not shoot at Baldr. Because I cannot see where he is, said Höðr, and I have no weapon. Loki said he should honour Baldr like the others, and offered to show him where Baldr stood. Höðr took the mistletoe and threw it as Loki directed; it pierced Baldr and he fell dead to the earth. It was, says Snorri, the greatest misfortune ever to befall gods and men.
sections.bodyZh: 霍德尔站在人圈的外面，因为他是瞎子。洛基走过去问他：你为什么不朝巴德尔扔东西？霍德尔说：因为我看不见巴德尔在哪里，而且我也没有武器。洛基说：你也该像别人一样向巴德尔表示敬意。我来给你指方向，你把这根树枝向他扔去吧。霍德尔接过槲寄生，照着洛基的指引朝巴德尔扔去。树枝穿透了巴德尔的身体，他倒在地上死了。斯诺里说：这是神和人所遭遇的最大不幸。

sections.bodyEn: When Baldr fell, the Æsir were struck dumb and their hands failed them to lift him. Each looked at the other, all of one mind about who had done the deed, but no vengeance could be taken there, for it was a place of great sanctuary. When they tried to speak, weeping came first, and none could tell the others his grief. Odin bore the loss worst of all, for he best understood how great a loss and ruin Baldr's death was for the Æsir.
sections.bodyZh: 巴德尔倒下的时候，阿萨众神都说不出话来，双手也失去了力气，不能把他扶起。他们彼此相望，心里都知道是谁干了这件事，却不能在那里报仇，因为那是一处圣地。他们想说话的时候，涌出的只有泪水，没有一个神能把自己的悲痛告诉别人。在所有的神中，奥丁最承受不住这个打击，因为他最明白，巴德尔的死对阿萨众神意味着多大的损失与毁灭。

sections.bodyEn: When the gods came to themselves, Frigg asked who among the Æsir would win all her love and favour by riding the road to Hel to find Baldr and offer Hel a ransom to let him come home to Ásgarðr. Hermóðr the Bold, Odin's son, undertook the journey. Odin's horse Sleipnir was led out, and Hermóðr mounted and galloped away.
sections.bodyZh: 众神稍稍平静之后，弗丽嘉开口问道：阿萨神族中有谁愿意赢得我全部的爱与恩宠，骑马走上通往冥界的路，去找赫尔，问她要多少赎金才肯让巴德尔回到阿斯加德？奥丁的儿子、勇敢的赫尔莫德说他愿意去。于是众神牵来奥丁的八足骏马斯莱布尼尔，交给赫尔莫德。他跃上马背，向冥界疾驰而去。这是众神在巨大的悲痛中想到的唯一办法：如果冥界的女王肯收下赎金，巴德尔也许还能回来。赫尔莫德的马蹄声远去了，而留在阿斯加德的众神，还要先为巴德尔送行。

sections.bodyEn: The Æsir carried Baldr's body to the sea. His ship Hringhorni was the greatest of all ships, but they could not launch it, so they sent to Jötunheimr for the giantess Hyrrokkin, who came riding a wolf with vipers for reins. Four berserks could hold the wolf only by knocking it down. She pushed the ship off with one shove, so that fire flew from the rollers and the earth shook; Thor would have smashed her head had the gods not begged for her. When Baldr was laid on board, his wife Nanna's heart burst with grief, and she was laid on the pyre with him. Thor hallowed the pyre with Mjöllnir and kicked the dwarf Litr into the flames; Odin laid the ring Draupnir on the pyre, and Baldr's horse was burned with all its harness.
sections.bodyZh: 阿萨众神抬起巴德尔的尸体，送到海边。巴德尔的船叫作“灵钟号”，是所有船中最大的一艘，众神想把它推下海，在船上为巴德尔举行火葬，可是船纹丝不动。他们只好派人到巨人之国去请一个名叫希罗金的女巨人来帮忙。她骑着一头狼来了，用毒蛇作缰绳。她跳下狼背，奥丁叫四个狂战士看住那头狼，他们只能把它摔倒才制服它。希罗金走到船头，只一推就把船推下了海，船底的滚木冒出火花，大地都颤抖起来。索尔大怒，握住锤子要打碎她的头，众神都为她求情，他才住手。巴德尔的遗体被抬上船，他的妻子南娜看见了，悲痛得心都碎了，当场死去，也被放上柴堆一起焚烧。索尔站在火堆前用妙尔尼尔为它祝圣，一个名叫利特的矮人从他脚前跑过，索尔一脚把他踢进了火里。奥丁把金环德罗普尼尔放在柴堆上，巴德尔的马也带着全套马具被送上火堆。

sections.bodyEn: For nine nights Hermóðr rode through dark, deep valleys where he could see nothing, until he came to the river Gjöll and rode onto the Gjallarbrú, roofed with gleaming gold. The maiden who guarded the bridge, Móðguðr, asked his name and lineage: the day before, five companies of dead men had ridden over, yet the bridge thundered more under him alone, and he did not have the colour of the dead. He said he was riding to Hel to seek Baldr; she told him Baldr had crossed the bridge, and that the road to Hel lay downward and to the north.
sections.bodyZh: 赫尔莫德骑着马走了九天九夜，穿过幽深黑暗的山谷，什么也看不见，直到来到冥河耶尔河边，骑上了铺着闪亮黄金的耶尔桥。守桥的少女名叫莫德古德，她问他的名字和家族，说：昨天有五队死人从这座桥上过去，可是桥被你一个人震得比他们全体还响；而且你的脸色不像死人。你为什么骑马走在通往冥界的路上？赫尔莫德说：我要去冥界找巴德尔。你有没有在路上见过他？莫德古德说：巴德尔已经骑马过了耶尔桥。通往冥界的路，就在下面，往北边去。

sections.bodyEn: At Hel's gate Hermóðr dismounted, tightened the girth, remounted and spurred Sleipnir, who leapt clean over the gate. In the hall he saw his brother Baldr in the seat of honour, and stayed the night. In the morning he asked Hel to let Baldr ride home, telling of the gods' grief. Hel said she would test whether Baldr was as beloved as they said: if all things in the world, alive and dead, wept for him, he would return to the Æsir; but if any refused to weep, he would stay with Hel. Baldr gave Hermóðr the ring Draupnir to take to Odin as a keepsake, and Nanna sent Frigg a linen kerchief and Fulla a gold ring.
sections.bodyZh: 赫尔莫德一路骑到冥界的大门前，他跳下马，把马肚带勒紧，重新上马，用马刺一踢，骏马高高跃起，从大门上方越了过去，一点也没碰到。他骑到大殿前下了马，走进去，看见他的哥哥巴德尔坐在高座上。赫尔莫德在那里过了一夜。第二天早晨，他请求赫尔让巴德尔和他一起骑马回家，并告诉她阿萨众神为巴德尔哭得多么伤心。赫尔说：我要看看巴德尔是不是真的像人们说的那样受到爱戴。如果世上的一切东西，活的和死的，都为他哭泣，他就可以回到阿萨众神那里；可是只要有一样东西反对、不肯哭泣，他就得留在冥界。赫尔莫德起身告辞，巴德尔送他出殿，把金环德罗普尼尔交给他，让他带回去给奥丁作纪念；南娜也送给弗丽嘉一块亚麻头巾和其他礼物，还送给弗丽嘉的侍女富拉一枚金指环。

sections.bodyEn: Hermóðr rode back and told all he had seen and heard. The Æsir sent messengers throughout the world asking that Baldr be wept out of Hel. All things did so — men and beasts, the earth and stones, trees and every metal — as you will have seen these things weep when they come out of frost into warmth.
sections.bodyZh: 赫尔莫德骑马回到阿斯加德，把他的所见所闻原原本本地告诉了众神。于是阿萨众神派出使者走遍全世界，请求万物为巴德尔哭泣，好让他从冥界回来。万物都哭了：人和动物、大地和石头、树木和各种金属都哭了——斯诺里说，就像你看见这些东西从严寒中被拿到温暖的地方时，身上会凝出水珠来一样。使者们走遍了天上和人间，所到之处，没有一样东西不在流泪。众神满怀希望，以为巴德尔就要回来了。可是，就在使者们办完差事、踏上归途的时候，他们经过了一个山洞——

sections.bodyEn: As the messengers were returning, having done their errand well, they found a giantess sitting in a cave who called herself Þökk. They asked her to weep Baldr out of Hel. She answered: Þökk will weep dry tears for Baldr's burning; alive or dead, the old man's son was no use to me — let Hel keep what she has. Men believe she was Loki Laufeyjarson, who had done the Æsir the most harm. And so Baldr remained in Hel.
sections.bodyZh: 使者们完成了使命，正在回家的路上，看见一个山洞里坐着一个女巨人，她自称叫作索克。他们请她也为巴德尔哭泣，让他从冥界回来。她回答说：索克要流干的眼泪，为巴德尔的火葬哭泣。不论他是活着还是死了，我从这老头的儿子身上什么好处也没得到。让赫尔留着她已经得到的吧！人们都认为，这个女巨人就是劳菲之子洛基变的，他给阿萨众神带来了最多的灾祸。巴德尔就这样留在了冥界。
sections.headingEn: The giantess who would not weep
sections.uncertaintyNote: 斯诺里说“人们认为”索克就是洛基，这是传统中的认定，不是故事中直接揭穿的情节。

sections.bodyEn: The gods were so angry that Loki fled and built a house with four doors on a mountain so he could watch every way, and by day he often hid as a salmon in the Fránangr falls. Wondering how the gods might catch him, he knotted linen into a net — the first net — and when he saw the gods coming, threw it in the fire and leapt into the river. Kvasir, wisest of the gods, saw the shape of the net in the ashes, and they made one like it. Dragging the falls with Thor at one end, they drove Loki until he tried to leap over the net; Thor caught him in mid-air and held him by the tail, which is why the salmon tapers at the tail.
sections.bodyZh: 众神对洛基怒不可遏，洛基逃到一座山上，盖了一间有四扇门的房子，好向四面八方都能看见。白天他常常变成一条鲑鱼，躲进法拉南格瀑布里。他坐在屋里想：阿萨众神会用什么办法来抓瀑布里的鲑鱼呢？他拿起亚麻线，像人们后来做网那样结了一张网。这时他看见众神已经来到不远处，奥丁从高座上望见了他的藏身之处。洛基赶快把网扔进火里烧掉，跳进河中。最聪明的神克瓦西尔第一个走进屋里，看见火中网的灰烬，明白这是捕鱼的工具，众神就照着灰烬的样子结了一张网。他们来到瀑布边撒网，索尔握住一头，其余的神握住另一头。洛基几次从网下、从网上逃脱，最后一次他想跳过网逃向大海，索尔在空中一把抓住了他，他滑溜溜地往外挣，索尔紧紧捏住他的尾巴——据说正因为这样，鲑鱼的尾巴才变得那么细。

sections.bodyEn: The gods took Loki into a cave, set up three slabs on edge and bored a hole in each. They took his sons Váli and Nari (or Narfi); Váli was turned into a wolf and tore his brother apart, and with Nari's entrails they bound Loki over the stones — one under his shoulders, one under his loins, one under the backs of his knees — and the bonds became iron. Skaði hung a venomous snake above him so that its poison dripped onto his face. His wife Sigyn stands by holding a bowl under the venom, and when the bowl is full she goes to empty it; then the venom drips on his face and he shudders so violently that the whole earth shakes — what men call earthquakes. There he lies bound until Ragnarök.
sections.bodyZh: 众神把洛基带进一个山洞，竖起三块扁石，在每块石头上钻一个洞。他们抓来洛基的两个儿子瓦利和纳尔维，把瓦利变成一匹狼，狼把他的兄弟撕成了碎片。众神用纳尔维的肠子把洛基捆在三块石头上：一块抵着肩膀，一块抵着腰，一块抵着膝盖窝，那些肠子随后变成了铁。斯卡蒂拿来一条毒蛇，挂在洛基的头上方，让蛇的毒液滴在他脸上。洛基的妻子西格恩站在他身旁，手里捧着一只碗接住毒液；碗满了，她就走开去倒掉，这时毒液就滴在洛基的脸上，他痛得猛烈挣扎，整个大地都随之颤抖——这就是人们所说的地震。洛基就这样被捆着，一直躺到诸神的黄昏来临。

claims.statement: Baldr is killed by a shoot of mistletoe despite the oaths.
Frigg takes oaths from fire, water, metals, stones, plants and beasts not to harm Baldr, but not from the young mistletoe.
Frigg is Odin's wife and knows all fates, though she does not prophesy.
Gylfaginning presents Frigg as Baldr's mother in the account of his death.

events.summaryEn: Frigg is Odin's wife.
events.summaryZh: 弗丽嘉是奥丁的妻子。
events.titleEn: The goddess who knows all fates

events.summaryEn: Baldr has ominous dreams, so Frigg makes fire, water, iron and all metals, stones, earth, trees, sicknesses, beasts, birds and serpents swear not to harm him.
events.summaryZh: 巴德尔做了不祥的梦。

events.summaryEn: Believing Baldr unharmable, the gods amuse themselves by throwing things at him.
events.summaryZh: 众神以为巴德尔刀枪不入，便拿东西扔他取乐。

sections.bodyEn: Frigg is Odin's wife. Snorri says she knows the fates of all, though she does not speak them aloud.
sections.bodyZh: 弗丽嘉是奥丁的妻子。斯诺里说，她知道一切人的命运，只是从不说出来。
sections.headingEn: The goddess who knows all fates

sections.bodyEn: Baldr has ominous dreams, so Frigg makes fire, water, iron and all metals, stones, earth, trees, sicknesses, beasts, birds and serpents swear not to harm him. Only a young mistletoe shoot she thinks too small to ask.
sections.bodyZh: 巴德尔做了不祥的梦。弗丽嘉便去找火、水、铁和各种金属、石头、土地、树木、疾病、野兽、鸟和蛇，让它们都发誓不伤害巴德尔。只有长在英灵殿西边的一株小槲寄生，她觉得太小，没有让它发誓。

sections.bodyEn: Believing Baldr unharmable, the gods amuse themselves by throwing things at him. But the mistletoe that never swore is made into a dart, and Baldr is struck down and dies.
sections.bodyZh: 众神以为巴德尔刀枪不入，便拿东西扔他取乐。然而那株没有发誓的槲寄生被做成了投枪，巴德尔被它刺中而死。
sections.uncertaintyNote: 投掷者与幕后之人的情节将在后续批次逐段登记。

stories.canonicalTitle: The birth of Huitzilopochtli on Serpent Mountain
stories.editorialNote: 依据《佛罗伦萨手抄本》第三卷第1章（萨阿贡编纂，16世纪）；学者把这段故事与大神庙布局相联系属于解释层。
stories.summaryEn: While sweeping on Coatepec, Coatlicue picks up a ball of feathers, tucks it at her waist and conceives. Her daughter Coyolxauhqui, shamed, leads the four hundred brothers to kill their mother. As they reach the summit, Huitzilopochtli is born fully armed, beheads Coyolxauhqui and scatters the brothers.
stories.summaryZh: 科阿特利库埃在蛇山打扫时，一团羽毛飘落，她把它塞在腰间，因此怀孕。女儿科约尔沙乌基认为这是耻辱，带着四百个兄弟要杀死母亲。就在他们冲上山顶时，维齐洛波奇特利全副武装地出生，砍下科约尔沙乌基的头，把兄弟们赶散。
stories.titleZh: 蛇山上的诞生：维齐洛波奇特利

sections.bodyEn: Coatlicue lives on Coatepec. One day as she sweeps, a ball of feathers drifts down. She picks it up and tucks it at her waist — and so she becomes pregnant.
sections.bodyZh: 科阿特利库埃住在蛇山上。一天她打扫时，一团羽毛从天上飘下来。她把羽毛捡起来，塞在腰间——就这样怀孕了。
sections.evidenceNote: 《佛罗伦萨手抄本》第三卷第1章。

sections.bodyEn: Her daughter Coyolxauhqui tells her brothers, the four hundred Centzon Huitznahua, that their mother has shamed them and must be killed. Armed, they set out for Coatepec.
sections.bodyZh: 她的女儿科约尔沙乌基对兄弟们——四百个南方人——说：母亲让我们蒙羞，我们必须杀了她。于是他们全副武装，朝蛇山进发。
sections.evidenceNote: 《佛罗伦萨手抄本》第三卷第1章。

sections.bodyEn: From the womb Huitzilopochtli comforts his mother: do not be afraid, I know what to do. The moment the attackers reach the summit he is born, carrying shield, darts and dart-thrower.
sections.bodyZh: 腹中的维齐洛波奇特利安慰母亲：不要怕，我知道该怎么做。敌人冲上山顶的那一刻，他出生了，手持盾牌、投枪和投枪器。
sections.evidenceNote: 《佛罗伦萨手抄本》第三卷第1章。

sections.bodyEn: Huitzilopochtli cuts off Coyolxauhqui's head, and her body tumbles down the side of Coatepec. He drives the four hundred brothers from the summit, scattering them in every direction.
sections.bodyZh: 维齐洛波奇特利砍下科约尔沙乌基的头，她的身体沿着蛇山滚落下去。四百个兄弟也被他从山顶追得四散奔逃。
sections.evidenceNote: 《佛罗伦萨手抄本》第三卷第1章。
sections.uncertaintyNote: 学者认为这段叙事与大神庙的布局相呼应，属于解释，不写成事实。

stories.canonicalTitle: Quetzalcoatl and Titlacauan at Tollan
stories.editorialNote: 依据第三卷第2–5、14章的章节标题与概要；各章细节尚未逐段建模。
stories.summaryEn: Florentine Codex Book 3 tells of Quetzalcoatl, a great wizard at Tollan. Sorcerers come to him — among them Titlacauan, also called Tezcatlipoca — and their portents bring his glory to an end. As he departs, his followers freeze to death between two snow-capped volcanoes.
stories.summaryZh: 《佛罗伦萨手抄本》第三卷讲述图拉的大法师羽蛇神。巫师们来到他身边，其中一位叫蒂特拉卡瓦，也就是特斯卡特利波卡；他们带来的种种征兆让羽蛇神的荣光走向终结。羽蛇神离开时，随行的人在两座雪山之间冻死。
stories.titleZh: 图拉的羽蛇神与蒂特拉卡瓦

stories.canonicalTitle: Two gods on one pyramid — the Templo Mayor
stories.editorialNote: 现实遗址层：依据墨西哥国家人类学与历史研究所（INAH）遗址博物馆的公开说明；不推测坐标。
stories.summaryEn: Atop the Templo Mayor of Tenochtitlan stood two shrines: on the south, Huitzilopochtli, solar god of war and patron of the Mexica; on the north, Tlaloc, god of rain linked to agriculture. INAH says the first small temple was built at the city's founding in 1325 and was rebuilt and enlarged many times.
stories.summaryZh: 特诺奇蒂特兰的大神庙顶上并立着两座神殿：南边供奉太阳战神、墨西加人的守护神维齐洛波奇特利，北边供奉与农业相连的雨神特拉洛克。墨西哥国家人类学与历史研究所说，神庙始建于1325年，此后多次重建与扩建。
stories.titleZh: 一座金字塔上的两位神：大神庙

stories.canonicalTitle: Three Maya gods in stone, clay and glyph
stories.editorialNote: 三个版本分别来自联合国教科文组织遗产记录与大都会艺术博物馆的两份说明；不把玛雅与墨西加的羽蛇神合并。
stories.summaryEn: Three separate witnesses, one god each: Chichen-Itza's El Castillo is also called the Temple of Kukulkan; a Met plate shows the rain god Chahk waist-deep in water; and a Met exhibition presents the aged sky god Itzamnaaj and his bird avatar. They are read separately, not stitched into one myth.
stories.summaryZh: 三份独立见证，各讲一位玛雅神：奇琴伊察的卡斯蒂略金字塔又叫“库库尔坎神庙”；大都会博物馆的一只陶盘上，雨神恰克半身浸在水中；同一博物馆的展览介绍年老的天神伊察姆纳和他的鸟形化身。三份见证分开阅读，不拼成一个统一神话。
stories.titleZh: 石头、陶盘与文字中的三位玛雅神

stories.editorialNote: 依据 ETCSL 1.1.1 综合文本；植物与疗愈神的名单尚未逐项建模。

stories.editorialNote: 依据 ETCSL 1.8.1.5（版本A）；与后来阿卡德语史诗的情节分开保存。
stories.summaryEn: Gilgameš resolves to make his name in the mountains. His companion Enkidu warns that the mountains are Utu's concern, so the sun god must be told. Gilgameš prays, and Utu accepts his tears as a gift and grants him seven warriors as guides to face Ḫuwawa, the guardian of the mountains.

stories.canonicalTitle: Fuxi makes the eight trigrams
stories.editorialNote: 依据《系辞下》第二章；“包牺即伏羲”采用传统注疏的读法。
stories.summaryEn: The Xi Ci II says that when Baoxi (Fuxi) ruled in antiquity, he looked up at heaven and down at the earth, studied the markings of birds and beasts and the land, drew on his own body and on distant things, and first made the eight trigrams; he also knotted cords into nets for hunting and fishing.
stories.summaryZh: 《周易·系辞下》说：古时包牺氏（伏羲）治理天下，他抬头观察天象，低头观察地理，看鸟兽身上的纹理和各地的物产，近取自身、远取万物，于是开始画出八卦；他又把绳子打结做成网，用来打猎捕鱼。
stories.titleZh: 伏羲始作八卦

claims.statement: The trigrams are made to communicate with the virtue of spirit-like intelligence and to classify the dispositions of the myriad things.
Xi Ci II is the textual witness for Baoxi's making of the trigrams.
The passage writes 包犧; reading Baoxi as Fuxi follows the traditional commentaries, which list 庖犧 and 伏戲 as variant forms.
Thereupon he first makes the eight trigrams (於是始作八卦).
Xi Ci II opens its account of the ancient sages with Baoxi (包犧氏) ruling all under heaven.
He knots cords to make nets for hunting and fishing.
He looks up at the images in heaven and down at the patterns on earth, observes the markings of birds and beasts and what suits the land, and takes from his own body and from things afar.

entities.canonicalName: Xi Ci commentary of the Zhouyi

events.summaryEn: Xi Ci II lists the inventions of the ancient sages, and the first is Baoxi — usually written Fuxi in later texts.
events.summaryZh: 《系辞下》讲古代圣人的发明，第一位就是包牺氏——后世通常写作伏羲。
events.uncertaintyNote: “包牺”即“伏羲”是传统注疏的读法。

events.summaryEn: He looked up at the images in the sky and down at the patterns of the earth; he studied the markings of birds and beasts and what each land was suited for.
events.summaryZh: 他抬头观察天上的日月星辰，低头观察大地的形势；又细看鸟兽身上的花纹，看各地适合生长什么。

events.summaryEn: Thereupon he first made the eight trigrams — eight figures of three lines each — to communicate with spirit-like virtue and to sort the dispositions of the myriad things.
events.summaryZh: 于是他开始画出八卦——八个由三条线组成的符号，用来通达神明的德性，把万物的情状分门别类。

events.summaryEn: He also knotted cords into nets, which people used to hunt and fish.
events.summaryZh: 他还把绳子打结，做成罗网，人们用它打猎、捕鱼。
events.uncertaintyNote: 后续圣人的发明不在本故事范围内。

sections.bodyEn: Xi Ci II lists the inventions of the ancient sages, and the first is Baoxi — usually written Fuxi in later texts. In remote antiquity, it says, he ruled all under heaven.
sections.bodyZh: 《系辞下》讲古代圣人的发明，第一位就是包牺氏——后世通常写作伏羲。书里说，远古的时候，是他在治理天下。
sections.uncertaintyNote: “包牺”即“伏羲”是传统注疏的读法。

sections.bodyEn: He looked up at the images in the sky and down at the patterns of the earth; he studied the markings of birds and beasts and what each land was suited for. Near at hand he drew on his own body, and far off on all things.
sections.bodyZh: 他抬头观察天上的日月星辰，低头观察大地的形势；又细看鸟兽身上的花纹，看各地适合生长什么。近处，他从自己的身体取法；远处，他从万物取法。

sections.bodyEn: Thereupon he first made the eight trigrams — eight figures of three lines each — to communicate with spirit-like virtue and to sort the dispositions of the myriad things.
sections.bodyZh: 于是他开始画出八卦——八个由三条线组成的符号，用来通达神明的德性，把万物的情状分门别类。
sections.evidenceNote: 《系辞下》第二章“于是始作八卦”。

sections.bodyEn: He also knotted cords into nets, which people used to hunt and fish. The Xi Ci then moves on to later sages such as Shennong; this retelling covers only Baoxi's part.
sections.bodyZh: 他还把绳子打结，做成罗网，人们用它打猎、捕鱼。《系辞》接下来再讲神农等后来的圣人，这里只讲伏羲这一段。
sections.evidenceNote: 《系辞下》第二章“作结绳而为罔罟”。
sections.uncertaintyNote: 后续圣人的发明不在本故事范围内。

stories.canonicalTitle: The Yellow Emperor and Chiyou at Zhuolu
stories.editorialNote: 依据《史记·五帝本纪》；司马迁以史笔叙述，本站只登记文本所述，不作历史真实性断言。
stories.summaryEn: The Shiji's Annals of the Five Emperors say that as Shennong's house declined and the lords fought one another, Xuanyuan trained troops. Chiyou, the most violent, rebelled against the ruler's command; Xuanyuan levied the lords' armies, captured and killed him in the wilds of Zhuolu, and was honoured as Son of Heaven — the Yellow Emperor.
stories.summaryZh: 《史记·五帝本纪》说：神农氏衰落，诸侯互相攻伐，轩辕操练军队征讨不服者。蚩尤最为暴虐，作乱不听帝命。轩辕征召诸侯之兵，在涿鹿的原野擒杀蚩尤，诸侯于是尊他为天子，这就是黄帝。
stories.titleZh: 黄帝战蚩尤：涿鹿之战

claims.statement: As the house of Shennong declines and the lords attack one another, Xuanyuan trains troops to punish those who do not bring tribute.
The Annals of the Five Emperors are the textual witness used for the Zhuolu episode.
Chiyou is the most violent of the lords; he rebels and does not obey the ruler's command.
The Shiji introduces the Yellow Emperor as the son of Shaodian, surnamed Gongsun and named Xuanyuan.
He finally captures and kills Chiyou (遂禽殺蚩尤).
The lords all honour Xuanyuan as Son of Heaven in place of Shennong; this is the Yellow Emperor.
Chiyou is the opponent at Zhuolu.
The Yellow Emperor levies the lords' troops and fights Chiyou in the wilds of Zhuolu.

entities.canonicalName: Battle in the wilds of Zhuolu

events.summaryEn: The Yellow Emperor was the son of Shaodian, surnamed Gongsun and named Xuanyuan.
events.summaryZh: 黄帝是少典的儿子，姓公孙，名轩辕。
events.uncertaintyNote: 此前轩辕与炎帝在阪泉的三次交战本故事未展开。

events.summaryEn: Among the lords Chiyou was the most violent, and no one could subdue him.
events.summaryZh: 诸侯之中，蚩尤最为凶暴，没有人能制服他。

events.summaryEn: Xuanyuan called up the armies of the lords and fought Chiyou in the wilds of Zhuolu, and at last captured and killed him.
events.summaryZh: 轩辕征召各路诸侯的军队，在涿鹿的原野上与蚩尤交战，终于把蚩尤擒住并杀死。
events.uncertaintyNote: 涿鹿不在本站映射为现代坐标。

events.summaryEn: The lords all honoured Xuanyuan as Son of Heaven in place of Shennong: this was the Yellow Emperor.
events.summaryZh: 诸侯们都尊奉轩辕为天子，取代了神农氏，这就是黄帝。

versions.labelEn: Shiji, Annals of the Five Emperors
versions.labelZh: 《史记·五帝本纪》
versions.narrativeScope: 轩辕崛起、蚩尤作乱、涿鹿之战与尊为天子
versions.rightsNote: 古籍原文属公共领域；只发布篇章定位与独立白话概述。

sections.bodyEn: The Yellow Emperor was the son of Shaodian, surnamed Gongsun and named Xuanyuan. In his time the rule of Shennong had declined; the lords attacked one another and oppressed the people, and Shennong could not punish them. So Xuanyuan trained troops to subdue the lords who would not pay tribute.
sections.bodyZh: 黄帝是少典的儿子，姓公孙，名轩辕。他那个时代，神农氏的统治衰落了，诸侯互相攻打、欺压百姓，神农氏却无力征讨。轩辕于是操练军队，去讨伐不肯朝贡的诸侯。
sections.uncertaintyNote: 此前轩辕与炎帝在阪泉的三次交战本故事未展开。

sections.bodyEn: Among the lords Chiyou was the most violent, and no one could subdue him. Chiyou rose in rebellion and would not obey the ruler's command.
sections.bodyZh: 诸侯之中，蚩尤最为凶暴，没有人能制服他。蚩尤起来作乱，不听从帝王的命令。
sections.evidenceNote: 《五帝本纪》“蚩尤作乱，不用帝命”。

sections.bodyEn: Xuanyuan called up the armies of the lords and fought Chiyou in the wilds of Zhuolu, and at last captured and killed him.
sections.bodyZh: 轩辕征召各路诸侯的军队，在涿鹿的原野上与蚩尤交战，终于把蚩尤擒住并杀死。
sections.uncertaintyNote: 涿鹿不在本站映射为现代坐标。

sections.bodyEn: The lords all honoured Xuanyuan as Son of Heaven in place of Shennong: this was the Yellow Emperor.
sections.bodyZh: 诸侯们都尊奉轩辕为天子，取代了神农氏，这就是黄帝。
sections.evidenceNote: 《五帝本纪》“诸侯咸尊轩辕为天子”。
