stories.canonicalTitle: The Odyssey, Part 2: the homecoming
stories.editorialNote: 依据巴特勒 1900 年英文散文译本，按卷顺序讲述第十三至二十四卷。求婚人与不忠侍女被处死的情节保留，但不渲染细节；最后一卷的真伪与年代在古代就有争议，这里照通行本讲。
stories.summaryEn: The Phaeacians carry the sleeping Odysseus home to Ithaca. Athena disguises him as an old beggar; he lodges with his loyal swineherd Eumaeus and is reunited with his son Telemachus, back from Sparta. As a beggar he enters his own palace, where the old dog Argos knows his voice and the suitors abuse him. His old nurse recognises his scar, and Penelope announces a contest with Odysseus's bow. No suitor can string it; the beggar strings it easily, shoots through twelve axes and takes his revenge in the hall. Penelope tests him with the secret of their bed and husband and wife are reunited; he makes himself known to his aged father in the orchard, and Athena at last brings peace to Ithaca.
stories.summaryZh: 费埃克斯人把熟睡的奥德修斯送回伊塔卡。雅典娜把他变成一个衰老的乞丐，他先投宿在忠心的牧猪人欧迈俄斯的茅屋里，又和从斯巴达回来的儿子忒勒马科斯相认。他以乞丐的身份走进自己的宫殿，老狗阿尔戈斯认出了他的声音，求婚人却百般羞辱他。老奶妈从伤疤上认出了他，珀涅罗珀宣布用奥德修斯的弓举行比赛。没有一个求婚人能拉开那张弓，乞丐却轻轻上了弦，一箭射穿十二把斧头，然后在大厅里向求婚人复仇。珀涅罗珀用他们婚床的秘密试探了他，夫妻终于团圆；他又在果园里与年迈的父亲相认，最后雅典娜让伊塔卡恢复了和平。
stories.titleZh: 奥德赛 · 下部 归家

claims.statement: When the Phaeacians leave the sleeping Odysseus in Ithaca, Athena reveals herself, praises his cunning, helps him hide his treasure and disguises him as an old beggar.

The swineherd Eumaeus shelters the disguised Odysseus, refuses to believe his oath that Odysseus will return, gives him his own cloak and tells how he was kidnapped as a king's son and sold to Laertes.

Warned by Athena of the suitors' ambush in the strait, Telemachus leaves Sparta, takes the fugitive seer Theoclymenus aboard at Pylos, avoids the ambush by sailing at night and lands secretly on Ithaca.
In the swineherd's hut Athena restores Odysseus's form and he reveals himself to Telemachus; father and son weep together and plan the suitors' death in secrecy.
Entering Ithaca as a beggar, Odysseus is kicked by Melanthius and restrains himself; at the palace door his old dog Argos recognises his voice, wags his tail and dies after twenty years.
In his own hall the beggar Odysseus is struck with a footstool by Antinous, breaks the jaw of the beggar Irus in a boxing match staged by the suitors, and vainly warns the kindly Amphinomus to leave.
Washing the disguised Odysseus's feet, his old nurse Eurycleia recognises the boar-tusk scar from his youth on Parnassus; he silences her while Athena keeps Penelope from noticing.

Penelope tells the disguised Odysseus her dream of an eagle killing twenty geese, distinguishes the gates of horn and ivory, and announces a contest of Odysseus's bow and twelve axes; next day omens of the suitors' doom multiply.
No suitor can string the bow Iphitus gave Odysseus; having revealed himself to Eumaeus and Philoetius, Odysseus strings it like a lyre and shoots through all twelve axes.

From the threshold of his hall Odysseus kills Antinous with his first arrow, refuses Eurymachus's offer of compensation and, with Telemachus, the two loyal herdsmen and Athena's aegis, defeats the suitors, sparing the bard Phemius and the herald Medon.
After the killing of the suitors Odysseus forbids Eurycleia to exult over the dead, punishes the twelve disloyal maids and Melanthius, and purifies the house with sulphur and fire.
Penelope tests the returned Odysseus by ordering his bed moved; his angry account of the bed built on a living olive trunk, a secret only they know, convinces her and they are reunited.

As Hermes leads the suitors' souls to Hades, Odysseus finds his aged father Laertes working in his orchard; after testing him with a tale, he proves his identity by his scar and the trees Laertes once gave him.

When the suitors' kin led by Eupeithes attack Odysseus at Laertes's farm, Athena with Zeus's sanction and thunderbolt stops the fighting and, in the guise of Mentor, establishes lasting peace in Ithaca.

events.summaryEn: When Odysseus finished his tale the Phaeacians sat spellbound.
events.summaryZh: 奥德修斯讲完了他的漂泊，费埃克斯人都沉默不语，被他的故事迷住了。
events.uncertaintyNote: 神话地点不推测坐标。

events.summaryEn: Odysseus climbed to the swineherd Eumaeus's stone-walled yard with its oak stockade and twelve sties.
events.summaryZh: 奥德修斯沿着崎岖的山路走到岛上的高处，来到牧猪人欧迈俄斯的院子。
events.uncertaintyNote: 神话地点不推测坐标。

events.summaryEn: In Sparta Athena came to Telemachus's bedside: he must go home, for the suitors were devouring his house and his mother was pressed to marry Eurymachus; and the worst of them lay in ambush in the strait between Ithaca and Samos, so he must keep clear of the islands, sail by night, send the ship on to the city and spend the night with the swineherd.
events.summaryZh: 这时在斯巴达，雅典娜来到忒勒马科斯的床前，对他说：你不该再离家这么远了，求婚人正在吞食你的家产，你的母亲也受到逼迫，要改嫁给欧律马科斯。
events.uncertaintyNote: 神话地点不推测坐标。

events.summaryEn: At dawn, as Odysseus and the swineherd made breakfast, steps sounded in the yard and the dogs fawned instead of barking: it was his son.
events.summaryZh: 天刚亮，奥德修斯和牧猪人正在茅屋里生火做早饭，听见院子里有脚步声，狗却没有叫，反而围着来人摇尾巴。
events.uncertaintyNote: 神话地点不推测坐标。

events.summaryEn: Telemachus returned to the palace and told his mother Menelaus's news that Odysseus lived on Calypso's island, while the seer Theoclymenus declared that Odysseus was already in Ithaca, plotting ruin for the suitors.
events.summaryZh: 忒勒马科斯回到宫中，老奶妈和母亲看见他，又惊又喜。
events.uncertaintyNote: 神话地点不推测坐标。

events.summaryEn: Athena urged Odysseus to beg among the suitors to learn who was decent and who lawless — though she meant to spare none.
events.summaryZh: 雅典娜催促奥德修斯到求婚人中间去讨饭，好看清楚谁善良、谁邪恶——尽管她并不打算放过任何一个。
events.uncertaintyNote: 神话地点不推测坐标。

events.summaryEn: That night Odysseus and Telemachus carried the helmets, shields and spears from the hall into the storeroom while Athena lit their way with a golden lamp.
events.summaryZh: 夜里求婚人散去，奥德修斯和忒勒马科斯把大厅墙上的头盔、盾牌和长矛都搬进了储藏室，雅典娜举着一盏金灯为他们照明。
events.uncertaintyNote: 神话地点不推测坐标。

events.summaryEn: Penelope asked the beggar to read her dream: twenty geese she loved were eating grain when an eagle swooped from the mountain and broke all their necks; she wept, and the eagle returned, perched on the roof and said in a human voice that this was no dream but truth — the geese were the suitors, and he, once an eagle, was now her husband come home.
events.summaryZh: 珀涅罗珀又对乞丐说：请你为我解一个梦。
events.titleEn: The dream of the geese and the omens
events.uncertaintyNote: 神话地点不推测坐标。

events.summaryEn: With a bronze key handled in ivory Penelope opened the inner storeroom and took down the bow, a gift from Iphitus whom Odysseus had met as a young man in Messene and which he had left at home as a keepsake.
events.summaryZh: 珀涅罗珀用一把象牙柄的铜钥匙打开了深处的储藏室，从木钉上取下那张弓。
events.uncertaintyNote: 神话地点不推测坐标。

events.summaryEn: Stripping off his rags, Odysseus leapt onto the threshold with bow and quiver and poured the arrows at his feet: the contest was over; now for another mark no man had hit.
events.summaryZh: 奥德修斯脱下破衣服，拿着弓和箭袋跳上大厅的门槛，把箭倒在脚前，说：这场比赛结束了，现在我要射另一个从来没人射过的目标，愿阿波罗让我成功。
events.uncertaintyNote: 神话地点不推测坐标。

events.summaryEn: When the fighting was over not one suitor had escaped; they lay heaped in blood and dust like fish a fisherman has dragged onto the sand.
events.summaryZh: 战斗结束了，求婚人一个也没有逃掉，像渔夫从海里拖上沙滩的鱼一样，横七竖八地躺在血泊和尘土里。
events.uncertaintyNote: 原诗对不忠侍女与墨兰提俄斯的处死有具体描写；本篇只交代结果。

events.summaryEn: Weak-kneed with joy, Eurycleia woke Penelope: the beggar was Odysseus and had killed the suitors.
events.summaryZh: 老奶妈欢喜得两腿发软，跑上楼去，叫醒熟睡的珀涅罗珀：快醒醒，奥德修斯回来了，那个乞丐就是他，他把求婚人都杀了！
events.uncertaintyNote: 神话地点不推测坐标。

events.summaryEn: Hermes with his golden wand called the suitors' souls from the palace, and they followed him squeaking like bats past the stream of Ocean, the White Rock and the gates of the Sun to the meadow of asphodel, where the shades of Achilles and Agamemnon were talking.
events.summaryZh: 赫尔墨斯手执金杖，把求婚人的鬼魂召出宫殿，它们像蝙蝠一样吱吱叫着跟在他后面，经过大洋河、白岩和太阳的门，来到长着日光兰的草地。
events.uncertaintyNote: 神话地点不推测坐标。

events.summaryEn: News of the slaughter spread; the families carried off and buried their dead and shipped the island suitors home.
events.summaryZh: 求婚人被杀的消息很快传遍了全城，死者的亲属们哭喊着从宫中抬走尸体，各自安葬，又把别的岛上来的求婚人的尸体装上船，送回家乡。
events.uncertaintyNote: 第二十四卷的真伪自亚历山大里亚学者起就有争议，有人认为原诗止于第二十三卷夫妻团圆处。

versions.labelEn: Odyssey, Books XIII–XXIV (Butler translation, long retelling)
versions.labelZh: 《奥德赛》第十三至二十四卷（巴特勒译本，长篇讲述）
versions.narrativeScope: 回到伊塔卡、牧猪人的茅屋、父子相认、老狗阿尔戈斯、大厅里的乞丐、伤疤、鹅的梦、弓的比赛、复仇、床的秘密、拉厄耳忒斯、雅典娜的和平
versions.rightsNote: 巴特勒 1900 年散文译本属公共领域；本站发布按卷顺序的独立讲述。

sections.bodyEn: When Odysseus finished his tale the Phaeacians sat spellbound. Next day they loaded his gifts — tripods, cauldrons, gold and fine clothing — and at sunset he boarded and fell into a sleep deep as death. The ship ran faster than a hawk and at dawn reached the harbour of Phorcys in Ithaca, by a long-leaved olive tree and the cave of the nymphs; the sailors laid him sleeping on the shore with his gifts and left. Poseidon complained to Zeus and turned their ship to stone as it neared home. Odysseus woke in a mist Athena had spread and did not know his land. Athena came as a young shepherd and told him it was Ithaca; overjoyed, he still lied, posing as a fugitive from Crete. She laughed, took a woman's shape and teased him — even at home he could not give up his tricks; he was the cleverest of men, she of gods. The mist cleared and he kissed the ground. They hid the treasure in the cave and plotted the suitors' death; she withered his skin, thinned his hair, dimmed his eyes, dressed him in rags, and sent him to the swineherd while she went to fetch Telemachus.
sections.bodyZh: 奥德修斯讲完了他的漂泊，费埃克斯人都沉默不语，被他的故事迷住了。第二天，国王阿尔喀诺俄斯让众人把礼物——青铜的三脚鼎、大锅、金子和精美的衣服——搬上船。太阳落山时，奥德修斯告别了王后阿瑞忒，上了船。水手们划起桨，他在船尾沉沉睡去，那一觉就像死亡一样深沉，他忘记了所受的一切苦难。那条船跑得比鹰还快，天亮时就到了伊塔卡，停在海中老人福耳库斯的港湾里，港湾尽头有一棵长着长叶的橄榄树，树旁是水泽女神的山洞。水手们把熟睡的奥德修斯连同毯子抬上岸，把礼物堆在橄榄树下，就回去了。波塞冬看见费埃克斯人送走了他的仇人，向宙斯抱怨；那条船快要回到港口时，海神一掌把它变成了一块石头，牢牢地扎在海底。奥德修斯醒来，雅典娜用雾气笼罩了四周，他认不出自己的家乡，以为费埃克斯人骗了他，伤心地在海边徘徊。雅典娜变作一个年轻的牧人走来，告诉他这里是伊塔卡。奥德修斯心中狂喜，却不说真话，编了一个故事：说自己是从克里特逃来的，因为杀了人才逃到这里。女神笑了，变回一个高大美丽的妇人，抚摸着他说：你这个狡猾的人，即使在自己的家乡，也不肯放下你的谎话和诡计。我们两个都是最会想办法的：你在凡人中间以智谋著称，我在众神中间以智慧闻名。她驱散了雾气，奥德修斯认出了家乡，跪下来亲吻大地。他们把礼物藏进山洞，坐在橄榄树下商量怎样杀死求婚人。雅典娜用神杖一点，让他的皮肤起皱，头发脱落，眼睛昏花，身上披着破烂肮脏的衣服，变成一个衰老的乞丐，叫他先去找忠心的牧猪人，自己则到斯巴达去叫回忒勒马科斯。

sections.bodyEn: Odysseus climbed to the swineherd Eumaeus's stone-walled yard with its oak stockade and twelve sties. Four savage dogs rushed at him; he sat down and dropped his staff, and Eumaeus drove them off with stones: the gods had given him grief enough — his master wandered who knew where while he fattened swine for the suitors. He seated the beggar on brushwood and a goatskin, roasted two piglets and poured wine. The suitors ate the best hogs every day. When the beggar swore Odysseus would return that very month, Eumaeus would not believe it: vagrants told Penelope such tales for a cloak, and she wept. That stormy night the beggar told how once outside Troy, freezing without a cloak in an ambush, Odysseus had tricked a man into running to camp and leaving his; Eumaeus took the hint and covered him with his own great cloak. Later he told his own story — a king's son of the isle of Syrie, kidnapped by a Phoenician nurse and sold to Laertes, raised with Odysseus's sister — and the two talked late by the fire, consoling each other for their sufferings.
sections.bodyZh: 奥德修斯沿着崎岖的山路走到岛上的高处，来到牧猪人欧迈俄斯的院子。院子用石头砌成，四周围着橡木栅栏，里面有十二个猪圈。四条像野兽一样凶猛的狗冲了上来，奥德修斯机警地坐下，扔掉手杖。欧迈俄斯赶紧跑出来，用石头赶走了狗，说：老人家，差点让狗把你咬了，那我可就更添一桩伤心事了。神已经给了我够多的痛苦：我的主人不知在哪里漂泊，也许正在异乡讨饭，我却在这里为别人养肥他的猪，让那些求婚人吃。他把乞丐请进屋，铺上树枝和一张山羊皮让他坐，杀了两头小猪烤了，又给他斟酒。奥德修斯一边吃一边想着报复。欧迈俄斯告诉他，求婚人每天都要吃掉最肥的猪，主人的财产就要被他们耗尽了。奥德修斯说：我向你发誓，奥德修斯一定会回来，就在这个月里。欧迈俄斯不信：许多流浪汉为了讨一件衣服，都到女主人面前编造主人的消息，她听了就哭。主人恐怕早已死了，狗和鸟吃掉了他的肉。这天夜里风雨交加，很冷，乞丐想要一件斗篷，就讲了一个故事：在特洛伊城下的一个寒冷的夜里，他跟着奥德修斯埋伏，没带斗篷，冻得要死，奥德修斯想了一个办法，派一个人回营地报信，让那人脱下斗篷留给了他。欧迈俄斯听出了他的意思，笑着把自己的一件大斗篷给他盖上。后来，欧迈俄斯讲了自己的身世：他本是叙里亚岛国王的儿子，小时候被一个腓尼基的保姆拐走，卖给了奥德修斯的父亲拉厄耳忒斯，和奥德修斯的妹妹一起长大。这对主仆在火边谈到深夜，仿佛两个经历了许多苦难的人在互相安慰。

sections.bodyEn: In Sparta Athena came to Telemachus's bedside: he must go home, for the suitors were devouring his house and his mother was pressed to marry Eurymachus; and the worst of them lay in ambush in the strait between Ithaca and Samos, so he must keep clear of the islands, sail by night, send the ship on to the city and spend the night with the swineherd. Menelaus gave him a silver bowl, and Helen a robe of her own weaving for his future bride. As they mounted the chariot an eagle flew up on the right carrying a great white goose from the yard, and Helen read the omen: as the eagle seized the tame goose, so Odysseus would come home after long wandering and take vengeance — perhaps he was home already. At Pylos Telemachus went straight to his ship, and took on board Theoclymenus, a seer's descendant fleeing kinsmen of a man he had killed. With Athena's wind they slipped past the ambush by night, landed on another shore at dawn, and Telemachus set off alone, spear in hand, for the swineherd's hut.
sections.bodyZh: 这时在斯巴达，雅典娜来到忒勒马科斯的床前，对他说：你不该再离家这么远了，求婚人正在吞食你的家产，你的母亲也受到逼迫，要改嫁给欧律马科斯。快回去吧。可是要当心，求婚人中最凶恶的那几个在伊塔卡和萨墨岛之间的海峡里埋伏着，要在你回家的路上杀死你。你要远远地避开那些岛屿，夜里航行；上岸以后，先让同伴们把船开进城，你自己去找牧猪人，在他那里过夜。第二天一早，忒勒马科斯向墨涅拉俄斯告别。墨涅拉俄斯送给他一只银碗，海伦送给他一件亲手织的长袍，说：这是海伦的手艺，留给你将来的新娘在婚礼上穿。他们正要上车，一只鹰从右边飞来，爪子里抓着一只从院子里抓来的大白鹅。海伦解释这个预兆说：就像这只鹰从山上飞来，抓走了家养的鹅，奥德修斯也会在漂泊多年以后回到家里，向求婚人复仇——也许他已经回来了。忒勒马科斯回到皮洛斯，没有进城去见涅斯托耳，免得被老人留住，直接上了船。正要开船时，一个外乡人跑来求他带上自己：他叫忒奥克吕墨诺斯，是一个预言家的后代，因为杀了人，正被仇家追赶。忒勒马科斯收留了他。船趁着雅典娜送来的顺风连夜航行，躲开了埋伏的求婚人，天亮时在伊塔卡的另一处海岸靠了岸。忒勒马科斯让同伴们把船开进城去，自己拿着长矛，沿着小路，向牧猪人的茅屋走去。

sections.bodyEn: At dawn, as Odysseus and the swineherd made breakfast, steps sounded in the yard and the dogs fawned instead of barking: it was his son. Eumaeus dropped his bowls and kissed the young man's head, eyes and hands, weeping like a father welcoming an only son home after ten years. Telemachus sent him to tell Penelope secretly of his return. Athena then stood at the gate, visible only to Odysseus and the dogs, which whimpered and slunk away; with a touch of her golden wand she restored him — clean clothes, a tall frame, dark skin and a dark beard. Telemachus, awed, took him for a god and promised sacrifices. 'I am no god,' said Odysseus; 'I am your father, for whom you have suffered so much.' He kissed his son, his tears falling to the ground, and told him this was Athena's doing; they wept aloud, more shrilly than sea eagles or vultures robbed of their young. Then they planned: the suitors were over a hundred, but Athena and Zeus were ally enough. Telemachus was to bear any insult to the beggar, remove the weapons from the hall at his nod, and tell no one — not Laertes, the swineherd or Penelope.
sections.bodyZh: 天刚亮，奥德修斯和牧猪人正在茅屋里生火做早饭，听见院子里有脚步声，狗却没有叫，反而围着来人摇尾巴。奥德修斯说：来的一定是熟人。话还没说完，他的儿子就站在了门口。欧迈俄斯惊得手里的碗都掉了，跑上前去，亲吻他的头、他的眼睛和双手，流着泪，就像一个父亲迎接一个在远方漂泊了十年、终于回来的独生子。忒勒马科斯派欧迈俄斯进城，悄悄告诉母亲他平安回来了。屋里只剩下父子两人。这时雅典娜站在院子门口，只让奥德修斯看见她，那些狗也看见了，它们不敢叫，呜咽着躲到院子另一边去。女神向奥德修斯点头示意，他走出屋子，女神用金杖一点，他立刻恢复了原来的样子：穿着干净的衣服，身材高大，面色黝黑，下巴上长出了黑色的胡须。他回到屋里，忒勒马科斯吓了一跳，以为他是一位神，转过眼睛不敢看他，说：外乡人，你和刚才不一样了，你一定是天上的神，请你可怜我们，我们会给你献上祭品。奥德修斯说：我不是神，我就是你的父亲，你为了我受了那么多苦，忍受着那些人的欺侮。他亲吻儿子，眼泪流到了地上。忒勒马科斯起初还不敢相信，奥德修斯告诉他，这都是雅典娜的作为。父子两人抱在一起放声痛哭，哭声比海鹰或者被农夫掏走了雏鸟的秃鹫还要凄厉。哭过以后，他们开始商量：求婚人有一百多个，忒勒马科斯担心他们两人打不过。奥德修斯说：有雅典娜和宙斯帮助我们，难道还不够吗？他嘱咐儿子：明天回到宫里去，我扮成乞丐跟着来。他们怎样侮辱我，你都要忍着。我向你点头时，你就把大厅里的兵器都搬到储藏室去。这件事不要让任何人知道，连拉厄耳忒斯、牧猪人和你的母亲也不要告诉。

sections.bodyEn: Telemachus returned to the palace and told his mother Menelaus's news that Odysseus lived on Calypso's island, while the seer Theoclymenus declared that Odysseus was already in Ithaca, plotting ruin for the suitors. That afternoon Eumaeus led the beggar to town; at the fountain the goatherd Melanthius, driving fat goats to the suitors, cursed them and kicked the beggar, and Odysseus mastered his urge to dash him to the ground. At the palace door, on a heap of dung, lay Argos, the dog Odysseus had raised before he left for Troy and once hunted wild goats, deer and hares with, now neglected and full of fleas. Hearing his master's voice he knew him, wagged his tail and dropped his ears, but was too old to come to him. Odysseus wiped away a tear unseen and asked about the fine dog; Eumaeus said he belonged to a man who had died far away, and in his prime no beast could escape him. As Eumaeus went into the hall, Argos, having seen his master again after twenty years, died.
sections.bodyZh: 忒勒马科斯回到宫中，老奶妈和母亲看见他，又惊又喜。他把在斯巴达听到的消息告诉母亲：墨涅拉俄斯说奥德修斯还活着，被卡吕普索留在海岛上。跟着他回来的预言家忒奥克吕墨诺斯却说：奥德修斯此刻已经在伊塔卡了，正在打听消息，要给求婚人带来灾祸。下午，欧迈俄斯领着乞丐进城。在城边的泉水旁，他们遇见了牧羊人墨兰提俄斯，他正赶着最肥的羊去给求婚人吃，一看见他们就破口大骂，还走过来朝乞丐的屁股踢了一脚。奥德修斯心里盘算，是用手杖打死他，还是把他举起来摔死在地上，可是他忍住了。他们来到宫门口，门前的一堆粪上躺着一条狗，它叫阿尔戈斯，是奥德修斯出征特洛伊之前亲手养大的，那时人们常常带它去追捕野山羊、鹿和野兔。主人走了以后，再也没人照顾它，它就躺在门口的粪堆上，身上长满了虱子。这时它听见了奥德修斯的声音，认出了他，就摇了摇尾巴，垂下了两只耳朵，可是它已经老得走不动了，没法走到主人身边去。奥德修斯看见了，悄悄擦去了眼泪，不让欧迈俄斯看见，问道：这条狗躺在粪堆上真可惜，它的样子很好，不知道它从前跑得快不快？欧迈俄斯说：这是那个死在远方的人的狗。要是它还像主人去特洛伊时那样，你一定会惊叹它的速度和力气，不管多深的树林里，只要它追赶的野兽，没有一只能逃掉。可是现在它老了，女仆们也不管它。欧迈俄斯走进大厅，阿尔戈斯在二十年后又见到了主人，随即就死去了。

sections.bodyEn: Athena urged Odysseus to beg among the suitors to learn who was decent and who lawless — though she meant to spare none. Most gave him bread and meat, but Antinous cursed him and hurled a footstool that struck his right shoulder; Odysseus stood firm as a rock, brooding on revenge. Even the other suitors protested: he might be a god, for gods go about disguised as strangers watching men's wrongdoing. Penelope cursed Antinous and sent for the beggar; he answered he would come after dark. Then Irus, a hulking town beggar of great appetite and little strength, threatened to drag him out by the feet. The delighted suitors set up a boxing match, the prize a goat-paunch stuffed with fat and blood and the sole right to beg there. When Odysseus girded his rags, baring mighty thighs, shoulders and arms, Irus shook; one blow under the ear broke his jaw. Odysseus dragged him out and propped him by the wall to scare off pigs and dogs. When the kindly suitor Amphinomus toasted him, Odysseus solemnly warned him to leave before Odysseus came — but Athena had doomed him, and he stayed.
sections.bodyZh: 雅典娜催促奥德修斯到求婚人中间去讨饭，好看清楚谁善良、谁邪恶——尽管她并不打算放过任何一个。乞丐挨个向求婚人伸出手，大多数人都给了他一点面包和肉，只有安提诺俄斯骂他是讨厌的东西，抓起一只脚凳朝他扔去，正打在他的右肩上。奥德修斯像岩石一样站着没动，心里却在盘算复仇。其他求婚人也觉得过分了，说：安提诺俄斯，你打这个可怜的流浪汉，太不应该了。也许他是天上的神，众神常常装成外乡人的样子，在城市里察看人们是否守法。珀涅罗珀在楼上听说了，诅咒安提诺俄斯，派人去请这个乞丐来，想向他打听丈夫的消息。乞丐让人回话，等到天黑求婚人散了再去。这时，一个名叫伊罗斯的乞丐来了，他是城里出名的大胃王，个子高大，却没有力气，想把奥德修斯赶出门去，骂道：老头儿，滚出去，不然我就拖着你的脚把你扔出去！求婚人看见两个乞丐吵架，乐坏了，安提诺俄斯提议让他们比赛拳击，谁赢了就可以吃一只塞满油和血的羊肚，以后只让他一个人在这里讨饭。奥德修斯把破衣服束在腰间，露出了粗壮的大腿、宽阔的肩膀和结实的胳膊，求婚人都惊呆了，伊罗斯吓得浑身发抖。两人一交手，奥德修斯只朝他的耳朵下面打了一拳，就打碎了他的下巴，他满口是血，倒在地上乱蹬。奥德修斯拖着他的脚把他拖出院子，让他靠墙坐着，把手杖塞到他手里，说：你就坐在这里赶猪赶狗吧。求婚人中有一个叫安菲诺摩斯的，为人比较和善，敬了他一杯酒。奥德修斯郑重地劝他：奥德修斯就要回来了，你趁早离开这里吧。可是雅典娜已经注定他要死在忒勒马科斯的矛下，他心里不安，却没有走。

sections.bodyEn: That night Odysseus and Telemachus carried the helmets, shields and spears from the hall into the storeroom while Athena lit their way with a golden lamp. Penelope sat by the fire with the beggar and told of her shroud and how she could delay no longer. He called himself Aethon of Crete, brother of King Idomeneus, who had hosted Odysseus for twelve days on his way to Troy. To test him she asked what Odysseus wore; he described a double purple woollen cloak and a golden brooch showing a hound pinning a struggling fawn — the very cloak and brooch she had given her husband — and she wept. Odysseus was near, he said, among the Thesprotians, and would come this very month. She ordered his feet washed; he asked for a faithful old woman, and Eurycleia brought a basin. He turned from the firelight, remembering his scar: in youth, hunting on Parnassus with the sons of his grandfather Autolycus, who had named him, a boar's tusk gashed him above the knee. Feeling it, she knew him and let his foot fall; the basin overturned. Athena turned Penelope's thoughts aside, and Odysseus gripped the nurse's throat: did she want to destroy him? She swore to be silent as stone or iron.
sections.bodyZh: 夜里求婚人散去，奥德修斯和忒勒马科斯把大厅墙上的头盔、盾牌和长矛都搬进了储藏室，雅典娜举着一盏金灯为他们照明。珀涅罗珀下楼来，坐在火边，和乞丐交谈。她讲了自己织寿衣骗求婚人的事，说现在父母催她改嫁，儿子也长大了，她再也想不出办法了。乞丐说自己是克里特人，名叫埃同，是国王伊多墨纽斯的弟弟，当年奥德修斯去特洛伊时，曾经被风吹到克里特，在他家里住了十二天。珀涅罗珀想试探他，问奥德修斯那时穿着什么衣服。他说：他穿着一件双层的紫色羊毛斗篷，上面别着一枚金别针，别针上刻着一只猎狗用前爪按住一只挣扎的小鹿，人人看了都惊叹。珀涅罗珀听了哭起来，因为那斗篷和别针正是她亲手交给丈夫的。乞丐安慰她说：奥德修斯就在附近，在忒斯普洛托斯人的地方，他很快就会回来，就在这个月里。珀涅罗珀吩咐女仆给客人洗脚，乞丐说只要一个忠实的老妇人。于是老奶妈欧律克勒亚端来一盆水。奥德修斯连忙转身背对着火光，因为他想起自己腿上有一道伤疤，怕被认出来。那是他年轻时去外祖父奥托吕科斯那里——奥德修斯这个名字就是外祖父给他起的——在帕耳那索斯山上打猎，被一头野猪的獠牙在膝盖上方划开的伤口。老奶妈用手摸到了那道伤疤，立刻认出了他，手一松，他的脚落进铜盆里，盆翻了，水洒了一地。她又悲又喜，眼里含满泪水，摸着他的下巴说：你就是奥德修斯，我的孩子！她转头想告诉珀涅罗珀，可是雅典娜转移了王后的注意力。奥德修斯一把掐住老奶妈的喉咙，低声说：奶妈，你想害死我吗？不要声张，让神帮我除掉那些求婚人。老奶妈说：你知道我的心像石头和铁一样坚定，我绝不会说出去。

sections.bodyEn: Penelope asked the beggar to read her dream: twenty geese she loved were eating grain when an eagle swooped from the mountain and broke all their necks; she wept, and the eagle returned, perched on the roof and said in a human voice that this was no dream but truth — the geese were the suitors, and he, once an eagle, was now her husband come home. The dream was plain, said the beggar. But dreams, she answered, come through two gates, of horn and of ivory, and only those through horn come true. Tomorrow she would hold a contest: whoever could string Odysseus's bow and shoot through twelve axes in a row, as he used to, she would follow. Do not delay it, said the beggar; Odysseus would be home before they strung it. That night, watching the maids slip out to the suitors, his heart growled like a bitch over her pups; 'Endure, my heart,' he said, 'you bore worse in the Cyclops's cave.' At dawn Zeus thundered from a clear sky, and a woman at the mill prayed this be the suitors' last meal. Ctesippus hurled an ox-hoof at the beggar, and Theoclymenus cried that he saw walls dripping blood, ghosts thronging the porch and the sun blotted out; the suitors laughed.
sections.bodyZh: 珀涅罗珀又对乞丐说：请你为我解一个梦。我家里养着二十只鹅，它们从水槽里吃麦子，我看着它们很高兴。一只大鹰从山上飞来，用弯嘴咬断了它们的脖子，全都杀死了，我在梦里哭了起来。那只鹰又飞回来，落在屋檐上，用人的声音说：放心吧，这不是梦，是将要实现的真事。那些鹅就是求婚人，我从前是一只鹰，现在是你的丈夫，回来要让他们全都不得好死。乞丐说：这个梦再清楚不过了，奥德修斯亲口告诉了你结局。珀涅罗珀说：梦有两道门，一道是牛角做的，一道是象牙做的。从象牙门出来的梦是骗人的，从牛角门出来的梦会成真。我怕我这个梦不是从牛角门出来的。明天就是那个可恨的日子了，我要举行一场比赛：奥德修斯从前常把十二把斧头排成一行，从远处一箭射穿所有的斧孔。谁能拉开他的弓，一箭射穿十二把斧头，我就跟谁走，离开这个家。乞丐说：不要再推迟了，在他们拉开那张弓之前，奥德修斯就会回到这里。这一夜奥德修斯睡在门廊里，看见那些和求婚人厮混的女仆嘻嘻哈哈地出去，他的心像一条护着小狗的母狗一样狂吠起来。他捶着胸口说：忍耐吧，我的心，当年独眼巨人吃掉我的勇敢同伴时，你忍受过更可怕的事。第二天清晨，他向宙斯祈求预兆，晴朗的天空中立刻响起了雷声；一个正在推磨的老妇人也祈求说：愿今天是求婚人在这里吃的最后一顿饭。宴会上，一个叫克忒西波斯的求婚人朝乞丐扔了一只牛蹄。预言家忒奥克吕墨诺斯忽然惊叫起来：可怜的人们啊，你们的头和脸都被黑夜笼罩，墙上和梁上淌着血，门廊和院子里挤满了奔向冥府的鬼魂，太阳从天上消失了！求婚人却哈哈大笑，说他疯了。
sections.headingEn: The dream of the geese and the omens

sections.bodyEn: With a bronze key handled in ivory Penelope opened the inner storeroom and took down the bow, a gift from Iphitus whom Odysseus had met as a young man in Messene and which he had left at home as a keepsake. She wept over it, then brought it and a quiver of arrows into the hall. Telemachus dug a trench and set up the axes; he tried three times and would have succeeded on the fourth had his father not shaken his head. Suitor after suitor failed even after warming and greasing the bow; Eurymachus groaned at their shame before later generations, and Antinous proposed waiting until after Apollo's feast. Outside, Odysseus asked Eumaeus and the cowherd Philoetius where they would stand if Odysseus came home; when both swore loyalty he showed his scar, and they wept. Eumaeus was to give him the bow and have Eurycleia lock the women's doors; Philoetius was to bar the courtyard gate. Inside, Telemachus sent his mother upstairs, and the bow reached the beggar. He turned it over for worm-holes, then strung it as easily as a bard strings a lyre, and the string sang like a swallow. Zeus thundered, and from his seat he shot an arrow clean through all twelve axes.
sections.bodyZh: 珀涅罗珀用一把象牙柄的铜钥匙打开了深处的储藏室，从木钉上取下那张弓。这张弓是奥德修斯年轻时在墨塞涅遇见伊菲托斯，伊菲托斯送给他的礼物；他去特洛伊时没有带走，把它留在家里作为纪念。珀涅罗珀把弓放在膝上，失声痛哭，然后拿着弓和装满利箭的箭袋走进大厅，对求婚人说：谁能最轻松地给这张弓上弦，射穿十二把斧头，我就跟谁走。忒勒马科斯挖了一条沟，把斧头排成一行。他自己先试，三次都没拉开，第四次眼看就要成功了，奥德修斯向他摇了摇头，他就放下了弓。求婚人一个接一个地试，有的把弓放在火边烤热，用油脂擦软，可是谁也拉不开；欧律马科斯拉不开，羞愧地说：我们比奥德修斯差得太远，后代人听了也会耻笑。安提诺俄斯说：今天是阿波罗的节日，不该射箭，明天再比吧。这时，奥德修斯跟着牧猪人和牧牛人菲洛提俄斯走到院子里，问他们：如果奥德修斯回来了，你们站在哪一边？两人都发誓帮助主人。他就露出那道伤疤，说：我就是奥德修斯。两人抱住他痛哭。他吩咐他们：欧迈俄斯把弓递给我，然后让老奶妈锁上女仆们的门；菲洛提俄斯去拴上院子的大门。回到大厅，乞丐请求试一试，求婚人都很恼火，怕他真的拉开了，让他们丢脸。珀涅罗珀坚持让他试，忒勒马科斯却请母亲回楼上去，说弓是男人的事。欧迈俄斯把弓递给了奥德修斯。他仔细察看那张弓，看有没有被虫蛀坏，然后就像一个熟练的歌手给竖琴换弦那样，毫不费力地给弓上了弦，用右手拨了一下弦，弦声清脆，像燕子的叫声。求婚人脸色都变了，宙斯在天上打了一声响雷。奥德修斯就坐在椅子上，搭箭拉弓，一箭射穿了所有十二把斧头。

sections.bodyEn: Stripping off his rags, Odysseus leapt onto the threshold with bow and quiver and poured the arrows at his feet: the contest was over; now for another mark no man had hit. Antinous was raising a golden goblet, never dreaming anyone would dare strike at a crowded feast; the arrow pierced his throat, the cup fell and the table overturned. The suitors searched the walls for weapons that were gone and threatened the beggar for his 'mistake'. 'Dogs,' said Odysseus, 'you thought I would never come home, so you wasted my house and courted my wife, fearing neither gods nor men; now your doom is here.' Eurymachus blamed the dead Antinous, who had wanted the kingship, and offered twenty oxen's worth from each man; Odysseus refused, and shot him as he charged. Telemachus speared Amphinomus and fetched armour for his father, himself and the two loyal herdsmen. Melanthius smuggled arms to the suitors until the herdsmen caught him and strung him from a rafter. Athena came as Mentor, then sat as a swallow on a beam, and at last raised her aegis, and the suitors stampeded like cattle stung by gadflies. At Telemachus's plea Odysseus spared the bard Phemius and the herald Medon.
sections.bodyZh: 奥德修斯脱下破衣服，拿着弓和箭袋跳上大厅的门槛，把箭倒在脚前，说：这场比赛结束了，现在我要射另一个从来没人射过的目标，愿阿波罗让我成功。安提诺俄斯正举起一只双耳金杯要喝酒，他做梦也没想到，在这么多人的宴会上，竟有人敢向他下手。奥德修斯一箭射穿了他的喉咙，他倒下去，酒杯从手中落下，饭桌被踢翻，食物撒了一地。求婚人跳起来，在大厅里到处找武器，可是墙上的盾牌和长矛早已不见了。他们还以为乞丐是失手误伤，骂他说你死定了。奥德修斯怒视着他们说：你们这些狗东西，以为我再也回不来了，就吞食我的家产，逼迫我的妻子，既不怕天上的神，也不怕人间的报应。现在你们的末日到了！欧律马科斯说：如果你真是奥德修斯，这都是安提诺俄斯的罪过，他想当伊塔卡的国王，现在他已经死了，我们每个人都赔你二十头牛的财物。奥德修斯说：就算你们把全部家产都给我，我也不会住手。欧律马科斯拔剑冲来，被一箭射中胸膛；安菲诺摩斯冲上来，被忒勒马科斯从背后用长矛刺倒。忒勒马科斯跑到储藏室，拿来盾牌、长矛和头盔，父子二人和两个忠心的仆人都武装起来。牧羊人墨兰提俄斯从没关好的储藏室偷了武器给求婚人，第二次去时被牧猪人和牧牛人抓住，绑起来吊在房梁上。雅典娜先变作门托尔出现，后来又变成一只燕子落在梁上，最后在屋顶上举起了她那令人丧胆的神盾，求婚人吓得像春天被牛虻叮咬的牛群一样四处乱窜。歌手费弥俄斯抱着奥德修斯的膝盖求饶，说他是被迫为求婚人唱歌的，忒勒马科斯为他和传令官墨冬求情，奥德修斯饶了他们两人。

sections.bodyEn: When the fighting was over not one suitor had escaped; they lay heaped in blood and dust like fish a fisherman has dragged onto the sand. Eurycleia, summoned, saw her master among the dead like a lion that has fed on an ox, and began to cry out in triumph. Odysseus checked her: rejoice in your heart, but do not exult — it is impious to boast over the slain; the gods' doom and their own wickedness destroyed these men, who honoured no one who came to them, good or bad. Of the fifty women of the house, she said, twelve had been shameless, defying her and their mistress and consorting with the suitors. Odysseus made those twelve carry out the dead and wash the tables with sponges and water, and then had them put to death; Melanthius, who had armed the suitors, was punished too. The poem's punishments are harsh, a reflection of the epic world's vengeance on betrayal; this retelling records the outcome without dwelling on it. Then with sulphur and fire Odysseus purified hall, house and courtyard, and the loyal women came out with torches to embrace him, kissing his head, shoulders and hands; he knew them all and was moved to sweet weeping.
sections.bodyZh: 战斗结束了，求婚人一个也没有逃掉，像渔夫从海里拖上沙滩的鱼一样，横七竖八地躺在血泊和尘土里。奥德修斯叫忒勒马科斯去把老奶妈欧律克勒亚叫来。老奶妈看见满地的尸体，看见主人像一头吃饱了牛的狮子一样，满身血迹，站在尸体中间，忍不住要欢呼起来。奥德修斯制止了她，说：老人家，你心里高兴就好，不要欢呼。对着死人夸耀是不敬神的。这些人是被众神的命运和他们自己的罪行毁灭的，因为他们不尊重任何来到他们面前的人，不管是好人还是坏人。他问老奶妈，宫里的女仆有哪些背叛了他。老奶妈说：宫里有五十个女仆，其中十二个不知羞耻，不尊敬我，也不听女主人的话，和求婚人混在一起。奥德修斯命令这十二个女仆把尸体抬出去，用海绵和水把桌椅洗干净，然后处死了她们；那个把武器送给求婚人的墨兰提俄斯也受到了惩罚。按照原诗，这些惩罚是严酷的，反映的是史诗世界里主人对背叛者的报复，本篇只交代结果，不渲染细节。随后，奥德修斯让老奶妈拿来硫磺和火，熏遍了大厅、宫室和院子，把宫殿彻底清洗干净。忠实的女仆们举着火把从房里走出来，围着奥德修斯，亲吻他的头、肩膀和双手，欢迎他回家。奥德修斯一一认出了她们，心中涌起一阵想哭的甜蜜之情。
sections.uncertaintyNote: 原诗对不忠侍女与墨兰提俄斯的处死有具体描写；本篇只交代结果。

sections.bodyEn: Weak-kneed with joy, Eurycleia woke Penelope: the beggar was Odysseus and had killed the suitors. Penelope could not believe it — surely a god had punished them, and Odysseus was long dead. She came down and sat silent across from him by the fire, now seeing her husband, now a man in rags. Telemachus called her heart harder than stone. If this was Odysseus, she said, they had secret signs only they knew. Odysseus smiled. Bathed and made handsome by Athena, he sat again: a strange, hard-hearted woman; let the nurse make him a bed to sleep alone. Penelope tested him: Eurycleia should move the bed he had built out of the bedroom. He flared up: who had moved his bed? Only a god could, for it had a secret. A broad-leaved olive grew in the courtyard, its trunk thick as a pillar; he built the bedroom round it, then lopped the crown, trimmed the trunk into a bedpost and built the bed upon it, inlaid with gold, silver and ivory and laced with purple oxhide. Her knees gave way; weeping, she ran and threw her arms round him. Let him not be angry — she had always feared some smooth-tongued deceiver; now he had told the secret of their bed, which only they and one maid knew, and her heart believed. He wept, holding his faithful wife, glad as shipwrecked sailors who reach land at last. Athena held back the Dawn to lengthen their night, and they told each other all their years apart, and he told her of the prophecy that he must yet carry an oar inland to a people who do not know the sea, and sacrifice to Poseidon.
sections.bodyZh: 老奶妈欢喜得两腿发软，跑上楼去，叫醒熟睡的珀涅罗珀：快醒醒，奥德修斯回来了，那个乞丐就是他，他把求婚人都杀了！珀涅罗珀不敢相信：一定是哪位神被求婚人的罪行激怒，杀死了他们，奥德修斯早已死在远方了。她走下楼来，坐在火光里，坐在丈夫的对面，一句话也不说，一会儿觉得他就是丈夫，一会儿又因为他穿着破衣服而认不出他。忒勒马科斯责备母亲：母亲，你的心比石头还硬，哪个妻子会这样冷淡地对待离家二十年、受尽苦难才回来的丈夫？珀涅罗珀说：我的孩子，我的心惊呆了。如果他真是奥德修斯，我们之间有一些只有我们两人知道的秘密，我们能认出对方。奥德修斯笑了。他沐浴后换上干净的衣服，雅典娜让他显得更高大英俊，他回到妻子对面坐下，说：奇怪的女人，众神给了你一颗比谁都硬的心。奶妈，给我铺一张床吧，我一个人睡。珀涅罗珀就试探他说：欧律克勒亚，把他亲手造的那张床从卧室里搬出来，给他铺好。奥德修斯一听就生气了：是谁搬动了我的床？除非神亲自动手，谁也搬不动它。那张床是我亲手造的，有一个秘密：院子里原来长着一棵枝叶茂盛的橄榄树，树干像柱子一样粗。我围着这棵树砌起了卧室，盖上屋顶，装上门，然后砍去树冠，把树干削平做床柱，以它为基础造了床，用金子、白银和象牙镶嵌，再绷上染成紫色的牛皮。我不知道它是否还在原地，还是有人把橄榄树砍断了。珀涅罗珀听了，两腿发软，心都化了，哭着跑过去，搂住他的脖子，亲吻他的头，说：不要生我的气。众神让我们受苦，不愿让我们两人一起享受青春，一起走到老年的门槛。我一直害怕会有人用花言巧语来骗我。现在你说出了我们的床的秘密，那是除了你、我和一个侍女以外谁也不知道的，我的心终于相信了。奥德修斯抱着忠实的妻子哭了，就像在海上遇难、拼命游泳的水手终于看见了陆地一样。雅典娜让黑夜停留在西方，不让黎明女神驾着她的快马升起，好让这对夫妻有更长的夜晚。他们互相讲述了二十年来的经历，奥德修斯也告诉她，先知预言他还要扛着一支船桨，走到一个不认识船桨的地方，向波塞冬献祭。

sections.bodyEn: Hermes with his golden wand called the suitors' souls from the palace, and they followed him squeaking like bats past the stream of Ocean, the White Rock and the gates of the Sun to the meadow of asphodel, where the shades of Achilles and Agamemnon were talking. When the suitor Amphimedon told their end, Agamemnon cried: happy Odysseus, to win so virtuous a wife; Penelope's fame would never die and the gods would inspire songs for her, while his own wife had murdered him. On earth Odysseus, Telemachus and the herdsmen went out to Laertes's farm. Odysseus went alone into the orchard and found his father digging round a plant in a patched, dirty tunic, oxhide leggings, gloves against the thorns and a goatskin cap, heavy with grief. Weeping under a pear tree, he decided, as was his way, to test him first with a tale of having once hosted Odysseus; Laertes poured black dust over his grey head and wept, and Odysseus could bear it no longer: 'Father, I am he.' Asked for proof, he showed the boar's scar and named the trees Laertes gave him as a boy walking in the orchard — thirteen pear trees, ten apple, forty fig, and fifty rows of vines. Laertes's knees gave way and he fainted into his son's arms; reviving, he cried that the gods were still on Olympus, since the suitors had paid for their crimes.
sections.bodyZh: 赫尔墨斯手执金杖，把求婚人的鬼魂召出宫殿，它们像蝙蝠一样吱吱叫着跟在他后面，经过大洋河、白岩和太阳的门，来到长着日光兰的草地。在那里，阿喀琉斯和阿伽门农的鬼魂正在谈话。求婚人的鬼魂安菲墨冬讲了他们的结局。阿伽门农听了感叹道：奥德修斯，你真幸福，娶到了一个多么贤德的妻子！珀涅罗珀对丈夫多么忠诚，她的美名会永远流传，众神会让歌手们为她唱出动听的歌；而我的妻子却谋害了自己的丈夫。这时在人间，奥德修斯和忒勒马科斯、两个牧人出城来到拉厄耳忒斯的农庄。奥德修斯让其他人进屋准备饭菜，自己走进果园，去试探父亲。他看见老人正在一棵树下松土，穿着一件打满补丁的脏衣服，腿上绑着牛皮护腿，手上戴着手套防备荆棘，头上戴着一顶山羊皮帽子，满脸悲伤。奥德修斯站在一棵梨树下流泪，心里盘算着是马上抱住父亲，还是先用话试探他。他按照自己的习惯，先编了一个故事，说自己从前在远方招待过奥德修斯。拉厄耳忒斯听了，两手抓起黑色的尘土撒在自己花白的头上，痛哭起来。奥德修斯再也忍不住了，冲上去抱住父亲，亲吻他说：父亲，我就是你盼望的那个人，二十年后回到了家乡，我已经杀死了那些求婚人。老人要他拿出证据。他先让父亲看了那道野猪留下的伤疤，又说：我还能告诉你，我小时候跟着你在果园里走，向你要树，你给了我十三棵梨树、十棵苹果树、四十棵无花果树，还答应给我五十行葡萄。拉厄耳忒斯听到这些确凿的证据，双膝一软，伸出双臂抱住了儿子，几乎晕倒，奥德修斯把他扶在怀里。老人苏醒过来，说：天父宙斯啊，众神确实还在奥林匹斯山上，那些求婚人终于为他们的罪行付出了代价！

sections.bodyEn: News of the slaughter spread; the families carried off and buried their dead and shipped the island suitors home. In the assembly Eupeithes, father of Antinous, cried for vengeance: this man had led away their young men and lost ships and crews, and now killed the best of the island; not to avenge sons and brothers would be eternal shame. The herald Medon and the old seer Halitherses warned that a god had helped Odysseus and that the fathers had failed to restrain their sons' wickedness; yet more than half took up arms behind Eupeithes and marched on Laertes's farm. Athena asked Zeus whether there would be war or peace; Zeus answered that Odysseus had his revenge — let them swear oaths, let him be king for ever, and let the gods make the kin forget the killing so that love, wealth and peace return to Ithaca. At the farm Odysseus, Telemachus, Laertes and old Dolius with his sons put on armour; Athena came as Mentor, and Laertes rejoiced to see son and grandson vie in courage. Given strength by Athena, he prayed and cast his spear through Eupeithes's helmet. As Odysseus and his son charged, Athena cried out to the Ithacans to stop the bloodshed, and they dropped their weapons and fled. When Odysseus pursued, Zeus hurled a thunderbolt at Athena's feet; 'Stop, son of Laertes,' she said, 'lest Zeus be angry,' and Odysseus gladly obeyed. Still in Mentor's shape and voice, Athena set a lasting covenant of peace between them.
sections.bodyZh: 求婚人被杀的消息很快传遍了全城，死者的亲属们哭喊着从宫中抬走尸体，各自安葬，又把别的岛上来的求婚人的尸体装上船，送回家乡。随后他们聚集在广场上，安提诺俄斯的父亲欧佩特斯悲痛欲绝，号召大家复仇：这个人先带走了我们的年轻人，丢了船，丢了同伴；回来又杀了我们岛上最优秀的子弟。我们要是不为儿子和兄弟报仇，就永远蒙受耻辱。传令官墨冬和老预言家哈利特尔塞斯劝阻他们：奥德修斯做这些事，有不死的神在帮助他；你们当初不听劝告，不阻止儿子们作恶，这是他们自己的罪过。可是多一半人还是拿起武器，跟着欧佩特斯向拉厄耳忒斯的农庄进发。雅典娜问宙斯：父亲，你打算让他们继续打下去，还是让双方和好？宙斯说：奥德修斯已经报了仇，让双方立下誓约，让他永远做国王；我们让死者的亲属忘掉儿子和兄弟被杀的事，让他们像从前一样相亲相爱，让伊塔卡充满财富与和平。农庄里，奥德修斯、忒勒马科斯、拉厄耳忒斯和老仆人多利俄斯父子一起穿上铠甲迎敌。雅典娜变作门托尔来到他们身边，拉厄耳忒斯欢喜地说：今天是多么好的日子，我的儿子和孙子在比赛谁更勇敢！雅典娜给了老人力量，他向宙斯和雅典娜祈祷后投出长矛，刺穿了欧佩特斯的头盔。奥德修斯父子冲向敌阵，眼看就要把他们全部杀死，雅典娜大声喊道：伊塔卡人，停止这场可怕的战争，不要再流血了！敌人吓得武器掉在地上，转身向城里逃去。奥德修斯还要追赶，宙斯降下一道雷电，落在雅典娜的脚前。雅典娜说：拉厄耳忒斯的儿子，足智多谋的奥德修斯，停下来吧，不要让鸣雷的宙斯发怒。奥德修斯欣然服从。于是，雅典娜仍然变作门托尔的模样和声音，让双方立下了永久和平的誓约。
sections.uncertaintyNote: 第二十四卷的真伪自亚历山大里亚学者起就有争议，有人认为原诗止于第二十三卷夫妻团圆处。
